articles.title: Xbox’s new disc-to-digital program gives physical games a digital future
articles.text:
For decades, console owners have faced a choice between the convenience of digital downloads and the permanence of physical game discs. Soon, Xbox owners will be able to get the best of both worlds for thousands of supported titles as part of a newly announced disc-to-digital program.
The program—announced today ahead of testing for Xbox Insiders starting August 31—will let players claim a “digital entitlement” for “most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games” simply by inserting the disc into a console and launching it. That game will then be playable completely digitally, without the need to ever insert the disc, as long as you (or a member of your family account) is logged in. The digital entitlement will also allow access to features like Xbox Play Anywhere (for play on PC) and Xbox Cloud Gaming, for supported titles.
Microsoft says that your physical disc will “continue to work exactly as it always has” after the digital entitlement is claimed. But before you get any ideas, the fine print on the announcement mentions that there is only “one revokable license per game disc,” so if you resell that disc or loan it to a friend, that digital entitlement could be transferred to a new account when someone else puts it into their console.
A leaked memo obtained by the Verge earlier this month suggests that publishers have to actively opt in to allow their game discs to activate digital entitlements, which could explain why “most” but not all Xbox One and Series X titles are supported. Windows Central separately suggests, based on discussion with unnamed sources, that “some discs may be incompatible due to how they were manufactured at the time,” which could explain why original Xbox and Xbox 360 discs are not being discussed for the program.

articles.title: Meta pagará más de 17 mil millones de dólares para resolver demanda por adicción de niños a sus redes sociales
articles.text:
Meta llegó a un acuerdo por casi 17.000 millones de dólares para resolver una serie de demandas presentadas por 29 estados en Estados Unidos, en las que la empresa era acusada porque Facebook e Instagram estaban diseñadas para generar adicción en niños y recopilación indebida de sus datos.
La compañía también se comprometió a implementar profundas modificaciones en el funcionamiento de sus plataformas orientadas a menores de edad. Este acuerdo pone fin al caso, que en un pricipio se estimaba podría solicitar un pago de 1,4 billones (1.400.000 millones) de dólares, una cifra que llevaría a la empresa a la quiebra.
PUBLICIDAD
El pacto surge tras un proceso judicial federal en California en el que 29 estados, entre ellos California, Colorado, Kentucky y Nueva Jersey, demandaron a Meta por diseñar deliberadamente productos adictivos para jóvenes, recopilar datos de menores sin el consentimiento de sus padres y engañar al público sobre la seguridad de sus plataformas.
Por qué Meta fue demanda por 29 estados en Estados Unidos
Las investigaciones que dieron pie a la demanda evidenciaron que Meta habría desarrollado características específicas en Facebook e Instagram para fomentar la adicción entre los menores de edad.
PUBLICIDAD
Los estados demandantes argumentaron que la compañía no solo diseñó estas funciones sino que ocultó deliberadamente su impacto negativo en la salud mental de sus usuarios jóvenes. Entre los problemas identificados se encuentran el aumento de la ansiedad, la depresión y, en algunos casos, la vinculación con conductas autolesivas y suicidio.
La demanda también acusaba a Meta de violar la Ley federal de Protección de la Privacidad Infantil en Internet, que prohíbe la recopilación de datos de menores de 13 años sin el consentimiento expreso de sus padres. Según los fiscales generales, la empresa recopiló datos personales de niños y adolescentes de manera sistemática, aprovechando la falta de controles efectivos para identificar la edad real de los usuarios.
PUBLICIDAD
A esto se sumó la denuncia de que Meta engañó a los consumidores al promocionar la seguridad de sus productos, a pesar de que sus propios ejecutivos tenían conocimiento interno de los riesgos que implicaban para los jóvenes.
Documentos internos y testimonios, como el del exdirector de ingeniería Arturo Béjar, indicaron que la prioridad de la empresa era maximizar el tiempo de uso y la frecuencia de interacción, colocando en segundo plano las advertencias sobre los potenciales daños psicológicos.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es el acuerdo de Meta para proteger a los menores de edad
El acuerdo alcanzado prevé el pago de más de 17.000 millones de dólares que Meta abonará a los estados demandantes a lo largo de diez años.
Esta cifra, aunque representa una pequeña fracción de los ingresos anuales de la empresa (201.000 millones de dólares en 2025), constituye uno de los mayores acuerdos en la historia de la protección al consumidor en varios estados, como destacó el fiscal general de Virginia, Jay Jones.
PUBLICIDAD
Además del pago, Meta se comprometió a una serie de transformaciones en la configuración y funcionamiento de Instagram y Facebook. Entre las principales medidas acordadas figuran:
- Límite diario de uso: se implementará un tope de dos horas diarias de acceso para menores de edad, con la posibilidad de que los padres lo ajusten.
- Bloqueo nocturno: las cuentas de menores quedarán bloqueadas entre la medianoche y las 6 de la mañana, salvo que un adulto responsable autorice lo contrario.
- Restricción de notificaciones: por defecto, la empresa no enviará notificaciones a los menores entre las 22 y las 7, extendiendo esta restricción al horario escolar durante el año lectivo.
- Controles parentales y de contenido: se reforzarán las herramientas para que los padres puedan supervisar el uso y la exposición de sus hijos, además de ocultar el número de “me gusta” y reacciones en las publicaciones de los menores.
- Eliminación de filtros de belleza: se prohibirán estos filtros en las cuentas de adolescentes, en respuesta a las críticas sobre su impacto en la autoestima y la imagen corporal.
- Desactivación de feeds personalizados: los jóvenes podrán optar por desactivar los algoritmos que personalizan el contenido mostrado, limitando la exposición a recomendaciones diseñadas para maximizar el tiempo de permanencia.
- Medidas de verificación de edad: se reforzarán los mecanismos de control para identificar con mayor precisión la edad de los usuarios y prevenir el acceso no autorizado de menores.
El acuerdo también contempla que, si otras redes sociales como Snapchat, TikTok o YouTube adoptan medidas similares, se reducirán aún más los límites diarios y las restricciones nocturnas.
PUBLICIDAD
El acuerdo pone fin a un juicio que amenazaba con consecuencias económicas aún mayores para Meta, ya que las sanciones potenciales podrían haber alcanzado hasta 1,4 billones de dólares.
Además, la empresa evitó exponer a su CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, a testificar ante el tribunal, al que sí asistió el jefe de Instagram, Adam Mosseri.
PUBLICIDAD
La resolución también evita que se sienten precedentes judiciales de mayor alcance sobre la responsabilidad de las plataformas digitales en la salud mental de los adolescentes, aunque marca un hito en la presión regulatoria sobre la industria tecnológica en Estados Unidos.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: OpenAI releases its official report on the Hugging Face breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI released its official report Wednesday on the Hugging Face breach, offering the clearest picture yet of how an unusual chain of events allowed an AI model to escape its testing environment and triggered a sprawling cybersecurity incident.
The report, released more than a month after the incident became public, spans several discrete cybersecurity compromises.
“This incident reflects misaligned behavior in an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events: the presence of impossible tasks in the ExploitGym evaluation, model persistence over long task horizons, and messages to peer models that caused those models to deviate from their goal,” the report reads.
Many of the details in OpenAI’s report were previously made public in a Black Hat presentation on August 6, but OpenAI’s official report gives a more thorough accounting of the incident, including more detail on the testing that initiated it. The report also gives critical new detail into how OpenAI aims to prevent future incidents, including chain-of-thought monitoring and a more advanced system for halting rogue agents.”
METR and Redwood Research also conducted third-party assessments of the models’ behavior during the incident; both groups are planning to publish their own reports on the incident.
In broad strokes, the report describes how an OpenAI model was presented with an unsolvable problem in testing and proceeded to chain together previously undiscovered exploits in order to bypass security measures and complete its task. The model initially compromised the Artifactory package management tool in order to gain access to the internet, then compromised various systems across OpenAI, Hugging Face, and other vendors.
The report gives critical new details about the models that carried out the breach. The primary model was from the same family as OpenAI’s forthcoming Astra model, although the report emphasizes that it was “a distinct model with different post-training, where much of a model’s behavior is shaped.”
Because OpenAI was testing the model’s capabilities, it was also unrestrained by the normal classifiers meant to prevent models from compromising digital infrastructure.
“OpenAI estimates maximal cyber capabilities by running this evaluation without the production classifiers intended to prevent models from pursuing high-risk cyber activity,” the report explains. “These evaluations are important so that OpenAI can measure models’ underlying capabilities and design appropriate safeguards.”
The report also gives significant new information about OpenAI’s security changes going forward, building on the heightened monitoring and alignment efforts made public last week.
In particular, the company is increasing its monitoring of AI agents’ “chain of thought,” a working space in which AI systems record short-term reactions and goals. That monitoring will be paired with 24/7 escalation systems, as well as new tooling to halt workloads that are deemed unsafe.
“These changes are intended to improve both the breadth and speed of detection — from infrastructure anomalies to potentially concerning model behavior — and pair that visibility with mechanisms for rapid containment,” the report states. “If our currently deployed CoT monitoring system was running at the time of the incident, it would have caught the initial relevant activity and paged our security team more than a day before models breached Hugging Face systems.”

articles.title: 'GTA 6' traerá de vuelta una función clave de 'San Andreas' que todos pedían
articles.text:
Rockstar ha confirmado una de las teorías más recientes sobre GTA 6. El estudio reveló que traerá de vuelta el sistema de peso y musculatura que hizo memorable a GTA San Andreas. Al igual que vimos con CJ, Jason y Lucía cambiarán físicamente según cómo los cuides durante la partida.
En una entrevista con Dazed, Rockstar detalló que GTA 6 contará con un sistema parecido al que vimos hace más de dos décadas en San Andreas. Tanto Jason como Lucía reaccionarán físicamente a las decisiones del jugador, por lo que si dejas que coman en exceso, ganarán peso de forma visible. En contraste, si vas al gimnasio y haces ejercicio, tu personaje se volverá más musculoso con el tiempo.
Esta es una de tantas teorías que circulaban sobre el juego desde hace meses. Varios jugadores analizaron las imágenes y los tráilers oficiales de GTA 6 y encontraron que Jason se veía más musculoso en algunas tomas y más delgado en otras. A eso se suma una imagen oficial en donde nuestro personaje levanta pesas en la playa, lo que sirvió para alimentar los rumores.
La buena noticia es que Jason y Lucía podrán volverse gordos como CJ. ¿Qué tanto? En realidad no sabemos si llegarán al nivel de obesidad mórbida que vimos en 2004, pero será notable. Lo interesante es que esta mecánica va más allá de la comida y el ejercicio, ya que los desarrolladores confirmaron que dormir poco, pasar demasiado tiempo huyendo de la policía o encadenar varios días de excesos afectará tanto el rostro como el cuerpo de los protagonistas.
Si comes mucho o te vas de fiesta, tu personaje de GTA 6 cambiará
Aunque esta opción es una de las más esperadas, Rockstar ha experimentado con mecánicas similares en sus últimos juegos. Basta ver a Red Dead Redemption 2, donde la barba crecía si no te afeitabas con regularidad, o los moretones que permanecían visibles durante días después de una pelea.
“Miramos atrás a nuestros juegos anteriores con ojo crítico y vemos hacia dónde queremos evolucionar basándonos en lo que no hicimos tan bien como nos hubiera gustado, ya sea porque no teníamos tiempo, recursos o capacidades tecnológicas, o en algunos casos cosas que simplemente no hicimos tan bien o no consideramos tan plenamente como podríamos”, dijo Rob Nelson, jefe de desarrollo y codirector del estudio en Rockstar North.
Además del aspecto físico, los desarrolladores revelaron que la relación entre Jason y Lucía tendrá un peso narrativo mucho mayor que cualquier otra dupla de personajes en la saga. Los jugadores podrán cambiar entre uno y otro de un modo similar a GTA V, aunque esta vez será necesario mantener una buena relación entre ellos para el desarrollo de la historia. Por último, GTA 6 integrará un feed de redes sociales para que los jugadores se distraigan cuando la vida en Leónida se vuelva rutinaria.
Rockstar tiene pensado mostrar un adelanto más amplio a través de un programa especial en Netflix. El vistazo extendido de GTA 6 se estrenará en la plataforma de streaming este jueves 27 de agosto a las 21:00 de España, las 16:00 de Argentina y las 13:00 de México. Hace unas horas, la compañía se pronunció sobre las filtraciones del juego e invitó a los fanáticos a que esperen un poco para no spoilearse la historia.

articles.title: Montech Titan PLA 750W power supply review: A powerful and stunning all-white Seasonic-built Platinum unit
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Montech Titan PLA 750W delivers exactly what its Seasonic pedigree promises: precise voltage regulation, outstanding ripple suppression, and thermal management that holds composure even under elevated ambient temperatures. The retail price at full MSRP is placing it at a disadvantage against the competition, but at a sale price it is one of the more complete and technically accomplished 750W offerings available today.
Pros
- +Seasonic platform
- +Genuine Platinum efficiency
- +Outstanding voltage regulation
- +Excellent ripple suppression
- +Full-bridge LLC topology
- +Great quality oarts
- +10-year warranty
- +Distinctive white dhassis
- +ATX 3.1 / PCIe 5.1 compliant
Cons
- -Costly at full price
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Montech is a Taiwanese PC hardware brand with deeper roots than its relatively recent public profile suggests. Founded in 2016 by engineers with over three decades of experience in Taiwan's PC industry, the company entered the Western market in 2019 with a value-focused positioning built around PC cases. Those cases sold well, and the catalog expanded quickly into power supplies, air coolers, liquid coolers, fans, and mechanical keyboards. The ambition from the beginning was to become a full-spectrum component brand rather than a niche case maker, and the PSU division is now central to that effort.
The earlier Century series established Montech's credentials in the mainstream segment, but the Titan PLA line represents a substantially higher level of commitment. Rather than sourcing from a mid-tier OEM and competing on price alone, Montech contracted Seasonic. That is not a trivial decision. Seasonic manufactures some of the best power supplies today and is widely regarded as perhaps the most consistently reliable OEM in the consumer PSU industry, responsible for technically accomplished designs under both its own brand and as the manufacturer behind multiple third-party lines. Montech prints the Seasonic name directly on the Titan PLA packaging, which communicates more about the product's engineering pedigree than any marketing copy could.
Specifications and Design
| Montech Titan PLA 750W ATX 3.1 Power specifications ( Rated @ 50 °C ) |  |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAIL | +3.3V | +5V | +12V | +5Vsb | -12V | 
| MAX OUTPUT | 20A | 20A | 62A | 3A | 0.3A | 
| Row 2 - Cell 0 | 100W | 100W | 744W | 15W | 3.6W | 
| TOTAL | 750W | Row 3 - Cell 2 | Row 3 - Cell 3 | Row 3 - Cell 4 | Row 3 - Cell 5 | 
| AC INPUT | 100 - 240 VAC, 50 - 60 Hz | Row 4 - Cell 2 | Row 4 - Cell 3 | Row 4 - Cell 4 | Row 4 - Cell 5 | 
| MSRP | $160 | Row 5 - Cell 2 | Row 5 - Cell 3 | Row 5 - Cell 4 | Row 5 - Cell 5 | 
In the Box
The Titan PLA 750W ships in a large, sturdy cardboard box with a restrained and effective visual theme - a black and polished metal aesthetic with a photograph of the unit printed on the front. The Seasonic OEM designation is printed openly on the packaging. For anyone with even a passing familiarity with the PSU market, that detail is more persuasive than any graphic design choice.
Inside the box, the PSU sits in a synthetic pouch surrounded by foam inserts. The accessory bundle is unexpectedly generous. We found mounting screws, an AC power cable, basic cable ties, five quality reusable cable straps, a set of cable combs, and an ATX jump-start adapter for testing. Few companies at any price point include all of that.
The cables are immediately distinctive. Bright white wiring runs throughout, paired with black connectors across the board. The wires feature an embossed braiding across their full length, giving them a slightly textured, uniform appearance that holds up well in windowed builds. The single 12V-2x6 connector is rated at 600W, which is the full ATX 3.1 specification requirement and not a given on a 750W unit. There are two 6+2 pin PCI Express connectors, which covers the most common configurations at this wattage tier but leaves no margin for extremes. It is a practical limitation worth noting before purchase.
| Montech Titan PLA 750W ATX 3.1 |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Connector type | Hardwired | Modular | 
|---|---|---|
| ATX 24 Pin | - | 1 | 
| EPS 4+4 Pin | - | - | 
| EPS 8 Pin | - | 2 | 
| PCI-E 5.0 | - | 1 | 
| PCI-E 8 Pin | - | 2 | 
| SATA | - | 8+2 | 
| Molex | - | 4 | 
| Floppy | - | - | 
External Appearance
At 160mm length, the Titan PLA 750W is marginally longer than the ATX design guide considers standard. Any quality modern tower case will accommodate it without difficulty, but it is worth verifying clearance in compact enclosures before ordering.
The chassis finish is satin white, excellently applied. A diagonally wired, chromed fan finger guard covers the intake, and chrome decorative elements extend to both side panels. The result is refined without being ostentatious. The top panel is home to a black electrical specification and certification sticker.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The front panel houses the standard power switch, AC receptacle, a small decorative plate, and a toggle switch for the hybrid fan mode. The rear modular connector bank is organized logically, with a subtle black legend identifying each port type. The ports are keyed anyhow, and inserting cables into the wrong connector is practically impossible.
Internal Design
Cooling relies on a Hong Hua HA13525H12F-Z 135mm fan with a fluid dynamic bearing (FDB) engine, rated to a maximum of 2300 RPM. That ceiling is high for a 750W unit and this unit should not need it, although the headroom is appreciated. FDB fans are a reasonable choice at a premium tier, balancing acoustic performance with long-term bearing reliability.
As noted, well, everywhere around the packaging and promotional material of this unit, the OEM is Seasonic. Founded in Taiwan in 1975, Seasonic has a vast reputation in the PC market. The company serves simultaneously as a retail brand and as the manufacturer behind several third-party labels, with past collaborators including Antec, NZXT, and XFX. The Vertex platform, launched in late 2022 as Seasonic's response to the ATX 3.0 and PCIe 5.0 standards, underpins the entire Titan PLA line. The Montech collaboration reportedly required 18 months of development before reaching production, and the unit was first revealed publicly at Computex 2024.
The filtering stage comprises four Y capacitors, two X capacitors, and two filtering inductors, which is a complete and adequate configuration. Two rectifying bridges sit on a dedicated heatsink immediately after the filtration stage.
The APFC stage uses two Infineon 6R190P6 MOSFETs and a CREE diode mounted on the unit's largest heatsink, with passive components consisting of a large encased inductor and two Nippon Chemi-Con 330 μF bulk capacitors. The primary inversion stage is where this design distinguishes itself most clearly from the competition, featuring four Infineon 6R230P6 MOSFETs arranged in a full-bridge LLC converter topology. Full-bridge LLC is a configuration far more commonly reserved for units above 1000W.
On the secondary side, four Nexperia PSMN1R4-40YLD MOSFETs generate the 12V rail via synchronous rectification. The tall secondary-side heatsinks are not in direct thermal contact with the MOSFETs, an unusual arrangement for top-mounted chips, though the thermal results indicate it presents no operational limitation. The 3.3V and 5V rails are derived from DC-to-DC converters on a vertical daughterboard, standard practice in any design of this caliber.
Secondary-side capacitors are almost entirely Nippon Chemi-Con, with a small number of Rubycon electrolytics. Both are Japanese manufacturers with long, consistent track records in the PC enthusiast community for durability and electrical stability. The component selection throughout reflects engineering priorities, not cost reduction.
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
Cold Test Results (25°C Ambient)
For the testing of PSUs, we are using high-precision electronic loads with a maximum power draw of 2700 Watts, a Rigol DS5042M 40 MHz oscilloscope, an Extech 380803 power analyzer, two high-precision UNI-T UT-325 digital thermometers, an Extech HD600 SPL meter, a self-designed hotbox, and various other bits and parts.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At 115 VAC, the Titan PLA 750W averaged 91.1% efficiency across the nominal load range. At 230 VAC, that figure climbed to 92.6%. Both results comfortably clear the Platinum certification thresholds under both Cybenetics and CLEAResult's 80Plus methodology. Efficiency stability is a particular strength here, as the curve holds level across most of the range, peaks near 50% load, and performs well even at low loads.
Fan behavior under cold conditions is excellent. The hybrid mode keeps the fan stationary at low loads and engages the fan once load surpasses roughly 30%, which is earlier than several competing designs allow. Audibility, however, remains minimal across most of the load range. There is a brief speed step approaching maximum output, but the fan does not approach its 2300 RPM ceiling under cold conditions. Internal temperatures are well controlled throughout.
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Hot Test Results (~45°C Ambient)
Under elevated ambient temperatures, average efficiency at 115 VAC falls to 89.8%, and 91.3% at 230 VAC. The degradation of more than 1% on average is measurable and slightly above the typical expectation, but no signs of thermal instability or output stress appeared at any load point during sustained testing. The platform handles thermal stress composedly.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Fan behavior expectedly shifts under heat but not as intensely as we are used to. Engagement drops to around 20% load, and the speed ramp is steeper than under cold conditions. The more noteworthy finding is that the fan barely exceeds the speeds it reached during cold testing, even at 100% output. That speaks directly to how well the thermal management architecture performs paired with a relatively stable efficiency design. Internal operating temperatures remain genuinely low across the entire load range.
PSU Quality and Bottom Line
Power Supply Quality
The electrical results are exceptional, with the unit delivering spectacular power quality. Voltage regulation sits at 0.5% on the 12V rail and 0.2% on both the 5V and 3.3V rails. Those figures are outstanding by any standard. Ripple suppression is equally clean, just 26 mV maximum on the 12V rail and 20 mV on both the 5V and 3.3V rails. These are numbers we infrequently get from top-tier products.
During our thorough assessment, we evaluate the essential protection features of every power supply unit we review, including Over Current Protection (OCP), Over Voltage Protection (OVP), Over Power Protection (OPP), and Short Circuit Protection (SCP).
All protection mechanisms, including OCP, OVP, OPP, and SCP, were verified and triggered correctly during testing. The OCP thresholds, however, are set very high: 158% on the 3.3V rail, 160% on the 5V rail, and 146% on the 12V rail. OPP triggered at 146% of rated output during hot testing. The unit sustained power delivery well beyond its 750W nameplate rating for significant time periods before shutting down. Rather than this being an issue and considering the platform, parts, and their ratings, it would seem that this unit deliberately carries substantially more headroom than the nameplate implies. The protection circuitry functions correctly - the thresholds simply reflect what this hardware is actually capable of.

Bottom Line
At the $160 MSRP, the Titan PLA 750W sits at the upper boundary of what the 750W segment will typically support. The competition at that price is real. At the $130 sale price it regularly appears at, the value calculation changes considerably. The electrical performance, component selection, and Seasonic engineering together produce a unit that easily competes technically against products priced $30 to $50 higher from comparable brands.
Taken as a whole, the performance profile of the Titan PLA 750W is difficult to fault. Voltage regulation figures comfortably outclass the majority of the competition at any wattage. Ripple suppression stays at or below 26 mV across all three rails under any load condition tested, including sustained full-load runs under elevated ambient temperatures. The efficiency figures meet the Platinum certification threshold with margin to spare and remain stable across the entire load range rather than peaking sharply at optimal points. Hot testing introduces a degradation which is measurable but entirely manageable, and critically, the unit shows no signs of thermal stress or output instability at any point during sustained high-load operation. The fan management is competent and audibility remains low for the overwhelming majority of real-world operating conditions. These are benchmark-level results and reflect the underlying platform more than any cosmetic or marketing consideration.
The advanced platform design and exceptional quality silicon used by Montech and Seasonic are what stands out about this series. The nearly exclusive use of Nippon Chemi-Con and Rubycon capacitors throughout the secondary stage reinforces that this product was not engineered down to a cost target.
Two 6+2 pin PCI Express connectors cover the most common use cases at this wattage, but the count could become a constraint for some builders. It is the most concrete criticism that can be leveled at an otherwise well-considered overall design. The 12V-2x6 connector is rated at 600W, the white cable aesthetic is genuinely distinctive and well executed, and the chassis finish is among the cleanest examples seen at this price point. The chrome accents could register as excessive depending on personal preference, but the underlying build quality is not in question.
The 10-year warranty is among the longest available in the consumer PSU market and reflects the confidence a Seasonic top-tier platform warrants. For a unit that will typically remain in service for about five years before the next significant system build, that commitment is not a marketing footnote but a meaningful feature that factors directly into total cost of ownership. Warranty length in the PSU segment correlates more reliably with platform quality than almost any other single specification, and a decade of coverage communicates something concrete about how Seasonic and Montech expect this hardware to age. The Titan PLA 750W is a product built by people who knew exactly which OEM to call, and the results confirm that the decision was correct.

articles.title: BYD adds 'Coming Soon' to Canadian website, posts 11 jobs
articles.text:
Chinese car company BYD has added ‘Coming Soon’ to its Canadian website, alongside job postings for 11 management roles.
On BYD’s website, Canada appears in the ‘American Region’ alongside Mexico, Brazil, and other Caribbean and Latin American markets. BYD also notes that it is present in more than 120 countries across six continents.
Now, the webpage doesn’t have any models, prices, dealer locations, an ordering function, or a launch date as of writing. However, as Electric Vehicles spotted, the contact details list BYD Canada Company Limited at 60 Travail Road in Markham.
Interestingly, the job postings that were found on LinkedIn include a head of sales, a sales manager, a marketing manager, a network development manager, an operations planning specialist, a legal counsel, and a human resources and administration manager. According to Electric Vehicles, three of those jobs were listed as actively reviewing applicants.
Interestingly, roles posted in Vancouver are listed as remote and appear under a separate Canadian entity; meanwhile, roles in Toronto are on-site, suggesting a head office.
There are also two things related to its automotive business shown off on its website: the FLASH charging system and its e4 platform. The charging system is advertised as being able to charge a battery from 10 per cent to 70 per cent in just 5 minutes, reaching 97 percent in only 9 minutes. In low-temperature performance, BYD says the duration from 20 per cent to 97 per cent only increases by a mere three minutes compared to room temperature.
The e4 platform, on the other hand, details an active safety system, integration with its second-gen “Blade” battery, and high-voltage Silicon Carbide Scaling.
It also lists the DMO hybrid system, which is paired with the 1.5-litre turbocharged engine, although it is unclear whether it will come to Canada.
This honestly doesn’t give us any new info, but it does show that we are getting closer to seeing BYD make its debut in Canada. I’m curious about the hybrid powertrain and if it makes a Canadian debut, mainly because I think that will be a way to sway traditional car buyers.

articles.title: This free Toronto art gallery spotlights some awesome local indie games
articles.text:
One Torontonian has come up with a cool way to shine a light on the city’s talented game development scene.
From illustrator, designer and art director Gavin McCarthy comes Art of the Concept, a free art gallery at George Brown Polytechnic’s North Gallery featuring Toronto indie games that debuted in partnership with this year’s annual Toronto Games Week. McCarthy has since extended the gallery, telling me that it will be there for the rest of August and at least partway into September until whenever the college needs the space once the new school year ramps up.
What an amazing turnout!
Thank you to everyone who came out to yesterday’s reception for Art Of The Concept. It was a wonderful afternoon filled with fantastic conversations about art and video games. A special thanks to the friends, family, volunteers and studios who helped make it happen
#TGW26
— artoftheconcept.bsky.social (@artoftheconcept.bsky.social) June 15, 2026 at 11:50 AM
In the exhibit, you can see key artwork from a bunch of Toronto games with some additional information on each alongside gameplay footage on adjacent TVs. Here are the nine featured games:
- Ambrosia Sky (Soft Rains)
- Astronomics (Numizmatic)
- Below (Capybara Games)
- The Big Con (Mighty Yell)
- Capy Castaway (Kitten Cup)
- Curse of Resthaven (Hilltop Studios)
- DuneCrawl (Alientrap)
- Echo Generation (Cococucumber)
- Neo Harbor Rescue Squad (BancyCo)
I unfortunately missed the gallery in June amid all kinds of other events (including FIFA, Dead by Daylight‘s 10th anniversary event and Game Con Canada), but I finally got to check it out this week and loved what I saw. Having this exhibit at a college that people, especially students, can just pop into at no cost is an excellent way to spotlight local indie games. I’ve long said we need more consumer gaming events in Canada to raise awareness of our world-class gaming industry, and Art of the Concept shows how grassroots efforts can very much help fill these gaps.
Shoutout to McCarthy for organizing this and to all of these talented teams for taking part. Definitely worth checking out if you’re in Toronto!

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 26, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 26, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, August 26, 2026.
From Girl Rising’s battle against gender stereotypes using cricket to AssessPrep’s data-driven revolution in the classroom, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Girl Rising’s RISE Premier League is using cricket to challenge gender stereotypes
On August 11, 2026, around 300 people gathered at the Government Higher Secondary School, Bhadi, in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, for something the village had never seen before—a cricket match in which girls and boys played together on the same team, as equals.
It was the opening match of the RISE Premier League (RPL) organised by non-profit Girl Rising as part of its flagship RISE education programme. The league features four mixed-gender teams and eight matches, and ends on October 10.
How AssessPrep is turning test scores into data schools can use
A test score tells a school how a student performed, but not necessarily where their understanding is strong or weak. AssessPrep, an assessment platform, tags every question to a topic and curriculum standard, allowing schools to see where an individual student or an entire class is falling short.
The platform, headquartered in Gurugram with operations in Jaipur, helps schools create, deliver, grade, and analyse tests, primarily for international curricula such as IB, Cambridge IGCSE, and Advanced Placement. It works with more than 800 schools, with an AI-first approach designed to save teachers time while giving schools more detailed data on student learning.
Latest news
Anaptyss bets on AI to drive value-led growth in BFSI
Anaptyss, the US-headquartered digital technology company with a significant presence in India, sees artificial intelligence (AI) as a key growth driver as it adds complementary capabilities to its existing portfolio of solutions.
Founded in 2021, Anaptyss has a strong focus on the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector, providing domain-led managed services to the industry. The company is now leveraging AI to expand its offerings and tap into new growth opportunities.
More than half of GCCs signal increased hiring in FY27: Report
The hiring outlook among global capability centres (GCCs) in India remains positive for FY27, although the focus is shifting towards hiring quality professionals rather than pursuing volume-led growth, according to a report.
The annual GCC survey by Taggd, in partnership with CII, titled From Intent to Predictable Scale: The Future of GCCs in India, found that 52% of GCCs plan to expand their workforce in FY27, up from 47% in the previous fiscal year.
Funding news
Emerald AI raises $150M at $1.05B valuation
Emerald AI, a US startup developing software that allows AI data centres to adjust their electricity consumption according to grid conditions, has raised $150 million in an oversubscribed Series A round at a valuation of $1.05 billion.
The financing was co-led by Energize Capital, an investment firm focused on the energy transition, and DCVC, a deeptech venture capital firm. The round also included strategic and financial investors such as NVIDIA, Samsung Ventures, Siemens, Aramco Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, GE Vernova, RWE, and JERA Ventures.
Ringg AI raises $10M in Series A led by Peak XV Partners
Bengaluru-headquartered voice artificial intelligence (AI) startup Ringg AI has raised $10 million as an extension to its Series A funding round, led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Arkam Ventures and Capital 2b. The startup had earlier this year raised $5.5 million as part of its Series A round.
The startup, which is also backed by Kunal Shah, was founded in October 2023 by Siddharth Shankar Tripathi (formerly with Groww and Flipkart), Utkarsh Shukla (ex-Blinkit and Atlan), and Kali CV (ex-Flipkart).
Scooby’s Club raises $250,000 to expand dog care network
Bengaluru-based dog care company Scooby’s Club has raised $250,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners. Founded in 2025, the company operates neighbourhood dog daycare, boarding and spa facilities, combining free-roam spaces with canine behaviour-led care.
The funding will support the opening of two additional Bengaluru properties over the next 6 to 12 months, alongside hiring and training canine coaches. Scooby’s Club plans to eventually build a network of 100 properties across major Indian cities. The company said its facilities include temperament-based grouping, climate-controlled indoor spaces, personalised care and 24-hour CCTV access for pet owners.
Cüraa raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A funding
Kitchen and lifestyle brand Cüraa has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with continued participation from Kae Capital, Lumikai and Better Capital. The company will use the funding to expand its pre-cook and cooking product portfolio, strengthen warehousing and supply chains, expand across D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce, and hire senior leadership.
Founded by Chef Sanjyot Keer and Neeraj Kumawat, Cüraa has served more than 3 lakh households since launching in September 2024. The company says its monthly net revenue has grown 25-fold since launch, with an average product rating above 4.5 and an NPS exceeding 70.
Other news
Chola Foundation provides flood relief to 1,250 Assam families
The Chola Foundation, in partnership with Smile Foundation, has provided flood relief across 10 affected regions in Assam, supporting more than 1,250 families. The intervention focused on essential and hygiene needs, with dry rations, hygiene kits and other supplies distributed to affected households, particularly women, children, elderly people and people with disabilities.
The relief effort was coordinated with local authorities and community leaders to identify affected communities. Chola employees in Assam also volunteered in the distribution of supplies, following safety guidelines issued by district authorities.
Octave opens Hyderabad technology centre with plans to hire 2,000 engineers
Octave Intelligence has inaugurated a 2 lakh sq ft Technology and Innovation Centre in Hyderabad, with plans to scale its engineering workforce to 2,000 in the coming years. The centre will support Octave's global operations across software engineering, AI, data, cloud and product development. It also houses an Experience Centre showcasing the company's industrial intelligence and AI solutions.
The facility is located in HITEC City and will develop technologies for customers across asset-intensive industries, including energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, utilities and transportation. Octave serves around 4,500 customers across 180 countries, including more than 60% of the Global Fortune 500.
Qure.ai appoints Mihir Bhanushali to lead global health expansion
Qure.ai has appointed Mihir Bhanushali as Executive Vice President, Global Health, to lead its expansion across low- and middle-income countries. Bhanushali joins from Freshworks, where he was Senior Director, Global Sales, and has previously held leadership roles at Rippling and Whatfix.
He will oversee growth across Africa, Southeast Asia, South Asia and Latin America, covering infectious disease programmes and frontline care delivery. Qure.ai's AI solutions are deployed across more than 107 countries and 5,200 sites. The company is also expanding beyond screening and diagnosis through Aira, its AI doctor and clinical co-pilot for frontline healthcare.
Vodafone Business, Tech Mahindra partner on UK digital transformation
Vodafone Business has partnered with Tech Mahindra to develop digital transformation solutions for UK enterprises. The collaboration combines Vodafone Business' enterprise connectivity and digital infrastructure with Tech Mahindra's expertise in AI, systems integration, digital engineering and managed services.
The companies will explore industry-specific solutions using AI, automation, private 5G, IoT, cloud and data to modernise operations, improve resilience and support new business models. The agreement includes executive engagement, co-innovation and joint go-to-market activities, with both companies identifying opportunities to address customer requirements and deliver measurable business outcomes.
Quest Global joins Babcock engineering services framework
Quest Global Engineering Services has been appointed to Babcock International’s Engineering Services Framework under a five-year agreement, expanding an existing collaboration between the two companies that began in 2023. The engagement covers Babcock programmes across Nuclear, Marine, Aviation, Land and Mission Systems. The agreement is part of Babcock’s strategy to build closer, long-term partnerships with key suppliers.
Quest Global will draw on its multidisciplinary engineering capabilities, outcome-focused delivery model and international experience across complex programmes. The partnership is expected to create opportunities to support initiatives focused on scale, operational performance, affordability and long-term resilience. Quest Global will work with Babcock and its wider ecosystem on projects spanning multiple domains and geographies, strengthening the scope of its engagement with the international defence company.
Foresight Law Offices launches DPDP compliance desk
Foresight Law Offices has launched a dedicated Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Desk and an interactive DPDP Readiness Assessment Tool to help organisations prepare for India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The initiative comes as businesses review their data practices ahead of the framework’s rollout. The DPDP Desk brings together the firm’s expertise across privacy, technology, cybersecurity, regulatory and corporate advisory.
Its services cover DPDP readiness, privacy and data governance frameworks, consent mechanisms, data principal rights, third-party data processing arrangements, data security and breach response. It also supports organisational policies and documentation while tracking regulatory developments. The interactive assessment tool provides organisations with an initial structured view of key considerations under the DPDP framework, helping them identify areas requiring attention as they prepare for compliance.
Client Associates appoints Siddharth Pardesi as chief business officer
Multi-family office and private wealth management firm Client Associates has appointed Siddharth Pardesi as Managing Partner and Chief Business Officer – HNI. Based in Mumbai, Pardesi will lead the company’s high-net-worth individual business as the firm builds on its position in wealth management. Pardesi brings more than two decades of experience across consumer banking, wealth management, investment products and advisory, as well as branch sales and distribution.
During his career, he has held senior roles at organisations including HSBC, BNP Paribas Sharekhan, Standard Chartered Bank and IndusInd Bank. His appointment is expected to strengthen Client Associates’ HNI business as it continues to engage with high-net-worth clients and expand its wealth management operations.
Embark named Major Contender in Everest Group assessment
Embark, an integrated service provider for Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India, has been named a Major Contender in Everest Group’s 2026 PEAK Matrix Assessment of GCC Setup Capabilities in India. The assessment evaluates providers on their ability to help enterprises establish GCCs, based on Everest Group’s annual Request for Information process, provider briefings and client reference interviews.
The recognition highlights Embark’s focus on GCC setup and enablement. Its model combines consulting, talent solutions, workspaces and enabling services to support companies establishing GCCs in India. Everest Group’s assessment also highlighted Embark’s Workforce Ramp Planning Toolkit and GCC Incubation-to-Scale playbook. These capabilities provide clients with a structured approach to achieving operational readiness and scaling their GCC centres.
Manish Dalal appointed NEN president
The National Entrepreneurship Network (NEN) has appointed Manish Dalal as President as it expands its efforts to enable entrepreneurs and businesses across India. Dalal brings more than 25 years of experience in general management, business development and international expansion across AI, SaaS and cloud businesses in the US and APAC markets. He joins NEN after holding senior leadership roles at technology companies including Motorola, Yahoo, Verisign, Endurance and Nextiva.
As President, Dalal will lead NEN’s entrepreneurship portfolio, covering programmes such as Wadhwani Ignite, Wadhwani Liftoff, Wadhwani Accelerate and WadhwaniEntrepreneur.ai. His responsibilities will also include Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship and Wadhwani SHG Micropreneurship. He will lead Wadhwani Government AI Platforms, which uses AI to support government programmes and improve livelihoods.
CureMeAbroad receives medical travel certification
CureMeAbroad, the medical tourism discovery and patient-navigation platform operated by Luxora Health Care Experiences, has received Medical Travel Facilitator Certification from Global Healthcare Accreditation (GHA). The certification strengthens the platform’s focus on safety, transparency and quality across the international patient journey. CureMeAbroad is now among a select group of medical travel facilitators globally certified under GHA’s programme for organisations that coordinate international patients with healthcare providers.
Unlike hospital accreditation, the certification evaluates organisations operating between patients and healthcare providers. It assesses leadership and accountability, patient services, risk management, business ethics, cultural and language support, staff training, financial and marketing transparency, and data protection. The certification comes as international patients increasingly rely on facilitators to navigate healthcare systems, compare treatment options and coordinate travel and post-treatment requirements.
Tribe Kombucha partners with Wow! Momo
Mountaintribe Foods, the maker of homegrown probiotic beverage Tribe Kombucha, has entered into a distribution partnership with Wow! Momo, one of India’s largest quick-service restaurant chains. Under the partnership, Tribe Kombucha will be made available across Wow! Momo’s network of more than 900 stores in over 100 cities across India. The company is scaling its distribution network as it prepares for its next phase of growth.
Blackbaud opens second Hyderabad office
Blackbaud, a provider of AI-powered solutions for social impact, has opened its second office in Hyderabad as it expands its operations in India. Located in the Financial District, the new facility is expected to support customers, product development initiatives and global operations while providing capacity for the company’s next phase of growth in India. Blackbaud expects its India workforce to continue expanding as it invests in future-ready talent and capabilities, including AI and cloud technologies.
Its existing HITEC City office houses Product Management, Enterprise Technology, Data Engineering and Research and Development teams. The new office will primarily support Blackbaud’s expanding Customer Operations organisation. Together, the two Hyderabad offices will support technology, customer and business functions, reinforcing India’s role as a collaborative delivery and support hub within Blackbaud’s global operating model.
Cashfree Payments launches AI agent Relay
Cashfree Payments has launched Relay, an AI-powered Super Agent designed to automate payment operations for small and medium-sized businesses and startups. Relay, which has been in beta with merchants since May 2026, is now available to all Cashfree merchants. According to Cashfree, seven in 10 Indian SMBs handle payment operations entirely manually, while most of the remainder use tools covering only a single channel or workflow.
Relay can execute tasks including retrying failed payments, following up on abandoned carts, confirming cash-on-delivery orders before dispatch, managing failed subscriptions and filing disputes ahead of deadlines. Cashfree said an average SMB spends 60 hours a week on payment operations, while Relay aims to reduce this to less than 45 minutes. The platform operates entirely on Cashfree infrastructure, with merchant transaction data not sent to external AI providers.
Fynd expands digital commerce platform for Woodland
AI-native retail technology company Fynd is powering the next phase of omnichannel growth for outdoor footwear and apparel brand Woodland by extending its unified Order Management System (OMS) and Warehouse Management System (WMS) across Woodland’s 171 stores and central warehouse operations. The integration is designed to improve inventory visibility, fulfilment agility and digital commerce operations. Woodland has integrated its store network and central warehouse operations on Fynd’s platform, creating a unified ecosystem across channels.
Fynd’s OMS enables omnichannel fulfilment and real-time inventory synchronisation across marketplaces including Myntra, AJIO, Flipkart, Nykaa, Nykaa Fashion and Tata Cliq. The connected platform integrates stores, warehouse, ERP, POS systems and digital channels. During peak sales periods, Woodland’s stores fulfil up to 2,500 orders daily, while the warehouse processes up to 2,000, creating a combined peak load of 4,500 orders.
Coverfox appoints Shikha Gupta as Chief Strategy Officer
Technology-led insurance distribution platform Coverfox has appointed Shikha Gupta as Chief Strategy Officer, effective July 1, 2026. Gupta will work with the leadership team to drive strategic growth, strengthen corporate partnerships and support Coverfox’s expansion across Bharat. She brings more than 18 years of experience spanning global finance, investing, financial services and portfolio leadership. Her areas of expertise include corporate strategy, capital allocation, mergers and acquisitions, governance and financial services.
Before joining Coverfox, Gupta served as Investment Director at Elevar Equity, where she evaluated investment opportunities across financial services, MSME lending, consumer businesses and insurance. Her appointment comes as Coverfox focuses on strategic growth and broader expansion. Gupta’s experience across investing and financial services is expected to support the company’s corporate partnerships and strategic initiatives.
Aziro launches enterprise AI agent platform Aziron
Aziro has launched Aziron, an enterprise agent execution platform designed to help organisations move beyond AI-generated answers and complete governed work. The platform brings agents, workflows, documents, models and enterprise tools together within a single governed environment. Aziron includes purpose-built modules for technical and business teams. Pulse focuses on engineering workflow automation, Atlas provides local-first code intelligence, Signal supports AIOps and incident reasoning, Canvas enables data apps and dashboards, while Harness provides model routing and cost control.
The platform is designed around governance, traceability and auditability. Aziron is now available as a self-hosted platform for on-premises deployment or customer-managed cloud environments. It also supports local models for private deployments, enabling organisations to retain greater control over their enterprise AI environments and data while using agents to execute business and technical workflows.
Matrix Geo Solutions completes 314-km highway survey
Geospatial technology and engineering consultancy Matrix Geo Solutions has completed a highway survey covering approximately 314 km across five road sections under LOT-2/HARYANA/Package-1. RITES Limited awarded the project on behalf of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
The assignment formed part of consultancy services for preparing a Detailed Project Report for economic corridors, inter-corridor and feeder routes aimed at improving freight movement efficiency in India. Matrix Geo Solutions was responsible for mapping physical, utility and land-related characteristics across the identified highway sections.

articles.title: Clavier, souris, écouteurs : Razer cède à la nostalgie des 25 ans de la Xbox avec une édition collector
articles.text:
Une souris Basilisk, un clavier BlackWidow et des écouteurs Hammerhead adoptent le vert translucide associé aux débuts de la Xbox. Razer joue à fond la carte de la nostalgie, mais avec des périphériques bien ancrés en 2026.
Le vert translucide des années 2000 revient sur les bureaux des joueurs. Pour les 25 ans de Xbox, Razer décline trois de ses périphériques phares dans une série limitée inspirée de la première console de Microsoft, avec livrée verte, éléments translucides et marquages commémoratifs.
Présentée pendant la gamescom 2026, la collection Xbox 25 Anniversary ne ressuscite toutefois pas les technologies de l’époque. Sous l’habillage rétro, tout reste très actuel.
Basilisk, BlackWidow et Hammerhead passent au vert
Les Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed ferment la marche avec une connexion sans fil 2,4 GHz à faible latence, du Bluetooth 5.3, une résistance IPX4 et jusqu’à 35 heures d’autonomie avec leur boîtier.
Razer annonce des tarifs respectifs de 179,99, 209,99 et 119,99 dollars. Les précommandes sont ouvertes sur la boutique américaine de Razer pour des expéditions à partir du 20 octobre. Les prix et la disponibilité en France restent à confirmer.
Un clin d’œil à la Xbox originelle
Le choix du vert ne doit évidemment rien au hasard. La première Xbox associait déjà sa grosse coque noire à un immense X et à un médaillon vert translucide devenu l’un de ses signes distinctifs.
Microsoft avait dévoilé sa console au CES 2001 aux côtés de The Rock, avant son lancement américain le 15 novembre de la même année avec Halo en porte-étendard. L’Europe avait dû attendre le 14 mars 2002.
La première Xbox avait aussi marqué les esprits avec son énorme manette, rapidement surnommée « Duke ». Un quart de siècle plus tard, les périphériques ont sérieusement fondu. Les prix, eux, ont beaucoup moins suivi le mouvement.

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude now has a browser of its own
articles.text:
Anthropic’s Claude now has a browser of its own
Anthropic is giving Claude its own browser.
As the company announced on Wednesday, Claude on the desktop (Mac, Windows, and Linux) now has access to a built-in Chromium-based browser in Cowork that allows it to surf the web right where you’re already doing your work.
This finally puts Anthropic’s Claude desktop app in line with OpenAI, which recently gave up its ambitions to build Atlas, its stand-alone browser, and instead added it to its ChatGPT desktop app.
This new feature is now rolling out to paying Pro, Max, and Team plan subscribers.
A browser, not your browser
Previously, for Claude to browse the web, you had to install a Chrome extension. That always felt a bit like a hack, though it worked reasonably well. But having used the ChatGPT app with the built-in browser — and the ability to quickly take screenshots in the browser and discuss them with the model — having a dedicated browser in these apps makes many workflows much easier.
Fun fact: the original Claude Chrome extension launched exactly a year ago, on August 26, 2025. It’s also only been two weeks since Anthropic launched a major update to the Chrome Extension, essentially turning it into a Cowork session. But the AI development cycle moves quickly, and two weeks is a very long time.
“Until now, giving Claude the ability to use the web in Cowork meant giving it access to your browser through the Claude in Chrome extension,” Anthropic explains. “When the work is on a page you already have open, that’s still the right choice. But a lot of web tasks don’t need your browser, just a browser, and now Claude has one.”
There is still a use-case for the Claude Chrome extension, though. It’s still useful to have Claude in the sidebar to talk about a page you have open in your browser.
“Claude in Chrome is for the page you already have open, with the accounts you’re already signed in to, such as updating your CRM, working through your inbox, or editing the doc in front of you,” Anthropic explains.
Also, if you have the extension installed already, it will remain the default for Claude to surf the web, unless you explicitly change your preferred browser in the Claude Desktop settings.
Bringing your logins across
The team notes this is very much “Claude’s browser, not yours.” But since it’s separate from your day-to-day browser, it doesn’t have your login info, for example. To work around that, Anthropic lets you bring your logins from Chrome, Edge, and Firefox on macOS — and Firefox on Windows and Linux.
The company very explicitly notes that logins from your banking and email providers, as well as any single sign-on sites, are explicitly excluded, unless you really insist on giving Claude access to your Schwab accounts.
The reason this list is inconsistent based on the operating system is likely that Chrome and Edge on Windows ensure that third-party applications can’t read your local cookies as an infostealer countermeasure. Firefox still stores these in a plain SQLite database. On MacOS, Chrome’s key is in Keychain, and other apps can request it from the user.
The risk is not zero
In this context, Anthropic also stresses that there is always a risk of prompt injections when letting an agent loose on the web. The company built safeguards into the Chrome extension and the built-in browser, but also notes that despite its best efforts, “the risk is not zero.”
Since the browser isn’t likely to be logged into many sensitive sites, if something goes wrong, the blast radius here is hopefully small.

articles.title: Queremos apagar el 2G y el 3G porque están obsoletos. El problema es que millones de coches y ascensores todavía no se han enterado
articles.text:
En 1991 la mayoría de la gente ni conocía los teléfonos móviles ni les importaban. Fue entonces cuando nació la tecnología 2G, que sentó las bases de una evolución frenética. En 2004 aparecerían las redes 3G, y aunque ambas lograron acabar por conquistarnos a todos y a todo, se quedaron obsoletas. Hoy en día ocupan un espectro de frecuencias que podría reutilizarse para mejorar la cobertura en redes 4G y 5G, pero hay un problema. O más bien, millones de ellos.
Los ascensores son un buen ejemplo. Muchos ascensores incluyen comunicadores que utilizan redes 2G o 3G para que una persona atrapada pueda contactar con el servicio de emergencia al pulsar el botón del ascensor. Esta opción ha funcionado durante años sin que nos diésemos cuenta de lo que la hacía funcionar: un pequeño módem móvil instalado en el ascensor. El apagado de las redes 2G y 3G obliga ahora a que comunidades y empresas de mantenimiento comprueben estos equipos y, en caso necesario, los arreglen reemplazando esos módems por otros compatibles con 4G.
Pero con los coches la cosa es peor. Desde abril de 2018 la Unión Europea exige que los nuevos tipos de turismos y furgonetas incorporen el sistema eCall, que es capaz de llamar automáticamente al 112 cuando detecta un accidente grave. También se puede accionar manualmente mediante el botón SOS que integran algunos coches, y gracias a ello además podemos enviar la posición del vehículo.
Difícil saber qué vehículos están afectados. El problema es que ese sistema se diseñó sobre la base de lo que eran las redes móviles disponibles en aquel momento: 2G y 3G. Así pues, aunque nuestro coche sea reciente, el sistema de soporte podría acabar desconectado sin más. Fabricantes como Seat, Volkswagen, Peugeot o Skoda ya disponen de comunicados oficiales en los que tratan de aclarar la situación a los consumidores explicando qué sistemas y modelos están o no afectados.
La UE reacciona. Un estudio encargado por la Comisión Europea y publicado en mayo de 2026 revela que hay 64 millones de vehículos expuestos, y la situación es tan preocupante que la UE ha decidido retrasar ese "apagón" de las redes 2G y 3G.
Problemón. Un módem 2G/3G no puede convertirse en uno 4G con una sencilla actualización de software. Aunque algunos fabricantes pueden ofrecer alguna alternativa, en muchísimos vehículos (y ascensores) la única alternativa será cambiar el hardware. En la Comisión Europea no esperan soluciones claras por parte de los fabricantes hasta 2030, así que desatascar esta situación parece especialmente complicado.
España ya está metida de lleno en esta transición. Hace años que Vodafone comenzó el apagado progresivo de las redes 3G, y Movistar también ha dado pasos hacia la retirada de esa cobertura. Otras operadoras manejan calendarios diferentes, pero el objetivo es común: liberar bandas de frecuencia que se puedan reaprovechar.
Una cara muy visible del problema (o mejor dicho, dos). Tanto los coches como los ascensores son los ejemplos más fuertes de la dicotomía a la que se enfrenta hoy en día el Gobierno de España. Durante años aprovechamos esa conectividad para conectar alarmas, terminales de pago, sistemas de teleasistencia, máquinas industriales, contadores, puertas o sistemas de seguimiento, además de todo tipo de dispositivos IoT. Muchos debían estar teóricamente preparados para durar años y años funcionando, pero este apagón compromete esa longevidad.
Morir de éxito. Llevamos despidiéndonos una década de las redes 2G, y aunque dicha tecnología pertenece más bien a una época pretérita, su enorme éxito hizo que la integráramos por todos lados. Ahora que queremos recuperar esas bandas de frecuencias, tenemos una dicotomía compleja entre manos: hay que actualizar millones de coches, ascensores y dispositvos IoT conectados para evitar males mayores. Hacerlo podría retrarar esa reasignación de bandas de frecuencias, y no está claro si al final lograremos mitigar este problema completamente.

articles.title: Renault 5 E-Tech : la version la moins chère s’améliore en France avec enfin la charge rapide, le carton de la rentrée ?
articles.text:
Renault 5 E-Tech : la version la moins chère s’améliore en France avec enfin la charge rapide, le carton de la rentrée ?
La Renault 5 E-Tech d’entrée de gamme s’améliore aussi en France. Charge rapide et batterie évoluent pour offrir leur lot de nouveautés en cette rentrée 2026, avec en prime deux nouveaux coloris.
Alors que Renault Allemagne a confirmé la bonne nouvelle la semaine dernière, le constructeur au losange officialise à son tour les évolutions de la Renault 5 E-Tech pour la France. Au programme : une autonomie revue à la hausse, la charge rapide généralisée, de nouveaux équipements et des teintes inédites. Seule ombre au tableau : contrairement à nos voisins germaniques, l'Hexagone ne profite d'aucune baisse de tarif à cette occasion.
La reine des citadines électriques européennes s'offre de nouveaux atouts
Afin d'aborder la rentrée du bon pied, toute la gamme de la Renault 5 E-Tech bénéficie d’une mise à jour bienvenue, tout particulièrement pertinente sur le modèle d’entrée de gamme. Ce dernier hérite enfin d’une recharge rapide de 80 kW, permettant de passer de 10 à 80 % de batterie en seulement 30 min. La puissance de charge en courant alternatif (AC) s'établit quant à elle à 6,6 kW (contre 11 kW auparavant).
Cette déclinaison adopte également un nouveau pack de batterie. Comme le pressentaient les rumeurs, Renault bascule vers la technologie LFP (lithium-fer-phosphate), déjà éprouvée sur la Twingo E-Tech. Si la capacité utile baisse légèrement à 36,5 kWh au lieu de 40 kWh, l’autonomie reste préservée et plafonne toujours à 305 km en cycle homologué WLTP.
Du côté des versions Autonomie urbaine (40 kWh) et Autonomie confort (52 kWh), le rayon d'action progresse grâce à un aérodynamisme retravaillé (nouveaux bas de caisse) et une gestion optimisée de la batterie. Leurs autonomies WLTP grimpent respectivement à 315 km et 430 km, contre 312 et 410 km jusqu'alors.
Plusieurs équipements inédits s'invitent dès la finition Techno. À l'instar des déclinaisons allemandes, la citadine intègre la recharge sans fil aimantée Qi2 pour smartphone, le mode de conduite Smart (qui bascule automatiquement entre les réglages Eco, Confort et Sport selon votre conduite) ou encore l’assistant vocal Gemini, qui remplace Google Assistant.
Deux teintes inédites font leur entrée : gris schiste métallisé et rouge flamme. Elles s'accompagnent d'un toit noir étoilé, de joncs de toit rouge alu ou Warm Titanium, ainsi que de stickers de toit et d’ailes Vibrant5 ou Hyper5. Enfin, des jantes Techno dorées apparaissent au catalogue des options sur les finitions Techno et Iconic Cinq, tandis que la sellerie de cette dernière passe désormais par défaut au bleu chiné en lieu et place du jaune.
Sur le plan tarifaire, la France ne bénéficie pas du même traitement de faveur que l’Allemagne puisque les prix y stagnent au lieu de baisser. La grille tarifaire de la Renault 5 E-Tech s'établit ainsi comme suit :
- Moteur 110 ch et batterie de 36,5 kWh (LFP) : 24 990 €
- 
120 ch et 40 kWh (NMC)
  - evolution : 28 490 €
  - techno : 30 490 €
- 
150 ch et 52 kWh (NMC)
  - evolution : 31 990 €
  - techno : 33 990 €
  - iconic cinq : 35 490 €
  - Roland Garros : 36 490 €

articles.title: Ethereum: cuál es la cotización de esta criptomoneda
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda virtual #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
PUBLICIDAD
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 120.7M de unidades creadas.
El precio de la criptomoneda de ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2452.5 dólares por unidad.
Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital reportó un cambio del -0.92 el último día, así como una variación del 0.0 % en la última hora.
PUBLICIDAD
Actualmente, ethereum se encuentra en el lugar #2 de popularidad en el mercado digital. Cabe mencionar que el máximo histórico que ha alcanzado esta divisa digital es de 4891.7 dólares por unidad.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Ethereum
La nueva era de Ether
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
PUBLICIDAD
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
PUBLICIDAD
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Faut-il avoir vu la série Dix pour cent avant d'aller voir le film sur Netflix ?
articles.text:
(Garantie 0 % spoiler : cet article ne révèle aucun élément de l’intrigue du film ni du final de la série).
Le piège classique des adaptations cinématographiques de séries télévisées est de s’adresser uniquement aux fans de la première heure. Bonne nouvelle : la créatrice Fanny Herrero et l’équipe du film ont conçu ce projet pour qu’il reste accessible au grand public. L’intrigue principale se focalise sur une mission d’urgence inédite, sauver le tout premier tournage d’Andréa, avec des enjeux propres au format cinéma.
Cependant, Dix pour cent repose intégralement sur une dynamique de groupe ultra-rodée, l’historique névrotique de ses agents et un réseau d’intrigues personnelles accumulées pendant quatre saisons. Débarquer à l’aveugle risque de vous priver de la moitié du plaisir et de la saveur des dialogues.
Le kit de rattrapage express : deux heures qui changent tout
Pour autant, ingurgiter l’intégralité des 24 épisodes de Dix pour cent n’est absolument pas nécessaire. La structure originale de la série reposant sur le principe un épisode = une péripétie avec une guest star, une immense partie des aventures passées s’avère totalement dispensable pour apprécier le film. Un programme de visionnage optimisé en deux temps suffit largement pour être parfaitement à jour.
Il convient tout d’abord de visionner deux ou trois épisodes de la première saison, à commencer impérativement par le pilote. Cette étape est cruciale pour comprendre le concept de l’agence ASK, assimiler le rôle de chacun et saisir l’essence même des personnages. C’est là que s’installent les dynamiques fondamentales : l’ambition dévorante d’Andréa, la duplicité de Mathias, la sensibilité de Gabriel ou la complicité entre Hervé et Noémie.
Il faut ensuite sauter directement aux deux derniers épisodes de la saison 4. Ce passage est indispensable pour faire l’état des lieux juste avant le film. Ces épisodes marquent la fin d’un cycle majeur pour ASK, montrent l’éclatement de l’équipe et posent les bases de ce que sont devenus les protagonistes. Sans ces éléments en tête, vous risquez de ne pas comprendre la situation dans laquelle se trouvent les personnages lorsque l’histoire reprend cinq ans plus tard.
Accessible aux néophytes, savoureux pour les préparés
En faisant l’impasse sur les saisons 2 et 3, vous manquerez évidemment quelques évolutions sentimentales ou professionnelles secondaires, mais le film prend soin de réinstaller rapidement le statut de chacun.
Le long-métrage qui sort le 10 septembre 2026 se regarde donc très bien de manière autonome grâce à son intrigue centrée sur le milieu du cinéma et ses apparitions de stars internationales. Mais consacrer deux petites heures à regarder le début et la fin de la série transformera une simple comédie sympathique en de vraies retrouvailles complices avec une bande d’agents inoubliable.

articles.title: Raspberry Pi now has an official guide for building your own cyberdeck
articles.text:
What just happened? In recent years, Raspberry Pi has played a major role in popularizing single-board computers as DIY products. Now, the UK-based organization has decided to promote an SBC-based cyberdeck that can be built using a few off-the-shelf components and offers plenty of customization options.
Raspberry Pi recently shared a series of DIY instructions for building a custom cyberdeck. The organization said the maker community has fallen in love with these homemade machines, which is why it has now published an "official" tutorial explaining how to build one using Raspberry Pi hardware and accessories.
By Raspberry Pi's definition, a cyberdeck is a computing device created from scratch, a purpose-built machine, or anything else designed to solve a specific problem. Cyberdecks occupy a niche filled with devices that can perform tasks traditional tablets or PCs cannot. However, we have also seen plenty of cyberdeck-like offerings that feel more like portable computers with custom designs than cyberpunk-inspired hacking devices.
Raspberry Pi's own idea of a cyberdeck is built inside a Pelican-style case, although the device could just as easily be housed in a wooden box, briefcase, or anything in between. Needless to say, the UK-based organization believes that a Raspberry Pi 5 single-board computer would be a perfect fit for the cyberdeck's "brain."
Other important components that form the basis of the custom-built machine include a 128GB Raspberry Pi Flash Drive, which is reportedly faster and more reliable than a standard microSD card, and a 7-inch Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2 with a 1,280 × 720 landscape resolution. The Rii RK302 Bluetooth keyboard has a low profile and fits almost perfectly inside the Pelican-style case.
Raspberry Pi also gave careful consideration to the question of power. While a cyberdeck can certainly run on batteries, the organization said that using a power bank makes the component layout easier and safer. There is also an option to add a Raspberry Pi RTC Battery, giving the cyberdeck real-time clock functionality.
The Raspberry Pi cyberdeck will require some soldering and gluing, but it should be accessible enough for DIY newcomers and computer enthusiasts who are not confident in their building skills beyond the Lego-like experience of assembling modern PCs. That said, the guide also feels somewhat like a cleverly crafted advertisement designed to sell more Raspberry Pi products to the maker community.
The tutorial was also featured in issue #168 of the Raspberry Pi official magazine, which can be read online for free. The magazine's print edition is apparently sold out already.

articles.title: Mad scientist makes LEDs in his backyard — semiconductor wizard who made his own RAM turns his attention to using bathroom eBay laser to etch sapphire wafers
articles.text:
Mad scientist makes LEDs in his backyard — semiconductor wizard who made his own RAM turns his attention to using bathroom eBay laser to etch sapphire wafers
It involves lasers!
The Dr. Semiconductor YouTube channel only has a few videos, but the man is quickly making a name for himself. He's built a semiconductor cleanroom in his backyard and made his own RAM cells there. Matthew Hartensveld (his real name) needs to figure out a way to package (cut and write) the RAM cells, so he figure he might as well use the opportunity to make some free-range, homemade LEDs while he was at it. This latest adventure is part of his open-source Semiconductor.DIY project.
The entire video is fascinating and information-dense, so we suggest you watch it to get the complete picture. Hartensveld started off with gallium nitride atop a sapphire wafer, that he proceeded to break into shards and clean with a solution including deionized water, acetone, and isopropyl. The primary goal was to etch the top layer of the material in order to define pattern contacts. Chlorine gas would be the obvious answer as that's what's used industrially, but it'd be more than a little hazardous in this setting.
The scientist turned his attention to a household item that makes every nerd happy: lasers. He ordered a powerful one from eBay, and moved it into his bathroom so his dog wouldn't look into it. Hartensveld quickly came across the problem that there was basically no information online about using said laser, and after a few attempts he managed to etch some scribbles on the wafer, and then actual patterns. After this, he test-drove the "LED" shard by smooshing some indium on it and using a 9 V battery, and lo and behold, there was blue light.
Doing so left a deposit of metallic gallium atop the pattern, so he came up with a solution to clean that up to leave the etched parts clearly exposed. Using a vacuum chamber with a two-stage pump that sucked out 99.999999% of the air out, he deposited a nickel/silver layer for the positive contact, then a titanium/silver for the N-contact and top metal, using argon plasma as the top gas. Even still, he later regretted not letting the chamber run for a while longer to draw out yet more air, to reduce residual gas.
At this point, Hartensveld had a fully working blue LED, though still in a wafer. That's right, blue, the color of LED that was a mystery for decades until a dedicated Japanese engineer figured it out. At any rate, the time came to package these LEDs, meaning cut them out of the wafer, and add physical connections. A table saw with very thin blades didn't really worked out, so in pure scientist fashion, Hartensveld turned once again to the laser, focusing it at a specific point to melt away the sapphire substrate. After an adjustment to make this a multi-passs process, he finally had a full cut.
The madlad still needed to add wire connectors, and after evaluating a few options, settled on indium bumps, the same method and material used in digital cameras. Last but not least, since he already had a blue LED on hand, he added a layer of cerium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (just bought off Alibaba) to add a yellow filter to end up with an ugly but functional white LED.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.
