articles.title: SpaceX will build a $100 billion Starbase in Louisiana, a 195-square-mile spaceport designed for thousands of annual launches
articles.text:
What we know so far: SpaceX has announced that it plans to build a new $100 billion spaceport on the Louisiana Gulf Coast, and to say it will be massive is an understatement. The company plans to construct the facility across 125,000 acres, or 195 square miles, in an area known as Pecan Island.
SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell said the facility, aptly named Starbase Louisiana, will be a self-sustaining spaceport with propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle-processing facilities, and even an airport.
The site is expected to house five launch complexes with two pads and a propellant farm apiece. That would make it SpaceX's fourth and largest launch site, with the capacity to support thousands of missions per year. Construction is due to begin in 2027, and the first launch is targeted for 2029, according to Louisiana Economic Development.
SpaceX likely chose the location for several reasons: its vast footprint provides room for expansion, the Gulf offers access to a wide range of launch trajectories, and Louisiana's abundant natural gas can supply both power and the methane used by Starship's Raptor engines. Deep-water access would also allow SpaceX to move the enormous vehicles and other hardware by ship.
 – SpaceX (@SpaceX) August 25, 2026
That ambitious launch rate depends on SpaceX making Starship rapidly and fully reusable. It was recently reported that the redesigned Starship V3 completed its first full test flight, while a 2024 milestone saw the company catch a returning Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's giant mechanical arms.
Starbase Louisiana would help launch Starlink satellites, missions to the Moon and Mars, and SpaceX's proposed orbital data centers – a plan that may involve up to one million satellites.
State officials expect the project to create 3,000 direct jobs over a decade with an average salary of $92,600, plus more than 8,100 indirect positions.
Louisiana has offered tax rebates and recruitment assistance, while SpaceX has agreed to make more than $820 million in local payments over 25 years and donate $25 million to a regional community foundation.
Unsurprisingly, the enormous scale of the development has raised plenty of concerns, especially when it comes to environmental implications.
The site occupies fragile coastal marshland close to protected wildlife areas, and residents and conservation groups fear the noise, light, traffic, and construction could harm fisheries, migratory birds, and wetlands that serve as a natural hurricane buffer. Many locals also say they were kept in the dark while officials negotiated the deal.
SpaceX's history suggests that people's concerns could be warranted. The company underestimated the blast effects of Starship's first integrated launch in Texas, which made a crater and scattered debris across the surrounding area. However, the Louisiana project will still face federal licensing and environmental reviews before rockets can fly.
SpaceX says it will develop only a small part of the property, leave large areas untouched, and work with state agencies to restore eroding marshland. It also plans to hold public town halls in the coming months.

articles.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash is cheap, good, and served on Chinese chips
articles.text:
Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash is cheap, good, and served on Chinese chips
Ox-alpha, the stealth model that quickly became the most popular model on OpenRouter in the last few days, is actually Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320 billion-parameter hybrid model (with 18 billion active parameters) that the team specifically trained for ultra-low-cost inference.
On Wednesday, Z.ai unmasked the stealth model and made its weights available on Hugging Face under the MIT license.
It’s also already available on a number of inference platforms, including OpenRouter, where it’s currently available at $0.075 per million input tokens and $0.25 per million output tokens (though those prices reflect a 50% discount).
Benchmarks: It’s good, but not Fable
While some of the early hype put the model at the level of Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5, the benchmarks don’t bear this out. But the model can, for the most part, keep up with a Claude Opus 4.8 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Terra when set to its max-effort reasoning mode.
On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, GLM-5.3-Flash sits at 57 points, in line with GPT-5.6 Terra, Google’s Gemini 3.7 Flash, Meta’s Muse Spark 1.2, and Qwen 3.8 2.4T A95B.
When it comes to its performance in driving AI agents, which may be a better indication of how it will perform in real-world use cases, it’s doing even better than its competitors.
The model is able to understand multimodal inputs, including images, videos, and files. Z.ai also stresses that it trained the model to do better at visual tasks like building presentations and websites, as well as at standard knowledge work tasks like working with documents, spreadsheets, and dashboards, all of which also benefit from the model’s improved visual capabilities.
One caveat: the model is very chatty and burns a lot of tokens, which isn’t unusual for smaller models that need more reasoning steps to achieve this kind of performance. Because the inference costs are so low, though, that’s not too much of an issue.
Cheap inference on Chinese chips
None of these competing models comes close to matching Z.ai’s pricing, and that may just be the most important takeaway from this launch. These Chinese open-weight models — including those from Alibaba, Deepseek, and Moonshot (Kimi) — are getting closer and closer to the performance of what American frontier labs can achieve — and they are making them available at a very low cost (and for free for those who have the hardware to run them).
One fact that tripped many early ox-alpha users up was the fact that the lab behind the model was able to serve 100 trillion free tokens per day (according to OpenCode). Very few infrastructure providers can handle that. But as it turns out, Z.ai did all of this on Chinese AI chips, something the company heavily stresses in its announcement.
“Compared with our initial baseline on the same hardware, we achieved a 3× improvement in end-to-end serving performance, reaching hardware efficiency and per-token cost comparable to mainstream NVIDIA GPUs,” Z.ai writes. “This demonstrates that Chinese chips can support frontier-model inference efficiently and economically at scale.”
Linear and sparse attention
The company doesn’t go into details, but notes that the individual chips are limited in compute and memory capacity. But Z.ai built its own inference engine based on SGLang for this serving stack — with the help of its flagship GLM-5.3 model powering an infrastructure agent, which the company says created “a feedback loop in which the model helped optimize the system serving the model itself.”
Z.ai doesn’t say what chips the model was trained on, but the company does note that it was trained on a 30 trillion multimodal pre-training corpus and that the team used a hybrid architecture that combines linear and sparse attention.
“Linear attention captures local dependencies through state modeling, while sparse attention retrieves relevant global context through a lightweight indexer,” the team explains, and also notes that compared to the full GLM 5.3 model, GLM 5.3-Flash’s architecture reduces the compute by 3x and KV cache size by 4.4x.
The model has a context window of 1 million tokens, so those reduced KV cache sizes make a substantial difference.
For developers, the calculus here is pretty straightforward. A model that matches Opus 4.8 on the benchmarks that matter for agents, at a tenth of the price, is hard to ignore. For the U.S. labs, the harder question is what happens now that Chinese labs can serve at this scale.

articles.title: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 Adds Durable and Verifiable Execution for AI Agents
articles.text:
Diagrid announced Catalyst 2.0 on 28 July 2026, adding failure recovery and cryptographic verification to agents built with frameworks including LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK and Dapr Agents.
Ten framework integrations ship in the release, also covering LangGraph Deep Agents, AWS Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Managed Agents, CrewAI and Pydantic AI.
Developers add a Diagrid package to an existing agent application. Diagrid says Catalyst then represents model and tool calls as durable workflow activities, allowing interrupted runs to resume without repeating completed work.
The failure mode this targets is a familiar one: a long multi-step run fails late in the sequence and, without checkpointing at call granularity, the retry re-pays for every model call already completed. Diagrid says Catalyst runs in cloud, on-premise and air-gapped environments. Durable agents are built with a Python SDK, while Catalyst's documentation lists workflow SDK support for .NET, Go, Java, JavaScript and Python; the open-source Dapr 1.18 SDKs also include Rust.
The verification model comes from Dapr 1.18. Dapr hashes batches of workflow-history events, links each digest to the preceding signature and signs the result using the Dapr sidecar's SPIFFE-based identity. The chain is checked when workflow state is loaded, making deleted, reordered or modified history detectable, and receivers validate each signed chunk against the Dapr Sentry trust anchor, so histories can be verified outside the application that produced them. Dapr groups the work as three capabilities: Workflow History Signing, Workflow History Propagation and Workflow Attestation, the latter two carrying verified execution context across workflow and service boundaries.
Teams should note that signing is disabled by default in Dapr 1.18, gated behind the WorkflowHistorySigning feature flag and dependent on mTLS, with daprd refusing to start if signing is enabled and mTLS is off. It is also a one-way decision per workflow: there is no retroactive signing of existing history, and toggling signing for a workflow already running is a verification error, so in-flight unsigned workflows must complete or be purged before enabling it more widely.
Yaron Schneider, Diagrid co-founder and CTO and chair of the Agentic AI Foundation's Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, said organisations need "proof of what happened" when agents call tools or delegate work.
Named early adoption is limited so far: optics manufacturer ZEISS Group is cited as an early user, with Wendelin Niesl, its head of end-to-end core application engineering, saying in the announcement that in "a rapidly evolving landscape of AI models and frameworks, Catalyst provides the stable foundation we can rely on", enabling the company to build "a sustainable, durable, and resilient platform for both AI and traditional workloads".
Catalyst is neither the first durability option for these frameworks nor a new entrant to a thin market. LangGraph persistence records checkpoints at graph superstep boundaries, supports resuming from a successful checkpoint and offers persistent task execution through its Agent Server, while Temporal and Restate provide replay or journal-based execution for long-running applications and can already host agent workflows. What sets Catalyst apart is a single Dapr-based recovery and attestation model spanning several frameworks, applying durability to individual model and tool calls rather than graph boundaries. The architectural decision is therefore where teams want recovery, identity, audit evidence and framework integration to reside.
Diagrid claims Catalyst can deliver up to ten times the performance of open-source Dapr and support millions of concurrent agent workflows. The announcement does not say whether that multiple refers to throughput, workflow starts per second or latency, nor which workload, hardware or Dapr configuration it was measured against, so the comparison cannot be independently assessed. Commercially, Diagrid publishes pricing spanning a free cloud tier, dedicated-cloud and bring-your-own-cloud plans sized by concurrent workflows, and a custom-quoted Enterprise Server edition for on-premise and air-gapped deployments.
Cryptographic attestation proves the integrity and provenance of recorded history, not that an agent made a correct decision, a tool returned accurate data, or every external side effect was captured. Practitioners should also assess retry handling for non-idempotent tools, storage and latency overhead, certificate rotation, independent verification, and which capabilities belong to open-source Dapr versus commercial Catalyst.

articles.title: Xtracycle's Swoop ASM e-bike brings an automatic transmission to cargo bikes
articles.text:
The Velotric Discover M e-bike we reviewed earlier this year had a feature I found somewhat annoying: It would sporadically block much of the display with an alert telling me I should be in a different gear. While the implementation bugged me, the concept made a certain degree of sense; most e-bikes now know your cadence, how much torque you’re generating, and how that power is being translated into speed. That’s everything you need to know to determine an optimal gear.
Somewhere in the back of my mind, I thought, “If you’re so smart, why don’t you just shift for me?”
I was completely unaware that Shimano had already developed a system that did exactly that. And for the past few weeks, I’ve been using it on a $4,500 cargo bike from Xtracycle called the Swoop ASM that let me see what it’s like to hand control of my gears to an electronic brain.
The short answer is that the electronics on the Swoop really are smart enough to figure out when it should be shifting. But the system is less adept at the actual shifting process, making for rides that are less smooth than they could be when it’s active. But you can shut that feature off, and the Swoop will shine as a fantastic cargo bike.
Swooping in
Xtracycle got its start providing cargo trailers for mountain bikes and then branched into dedicated cargo bikes. The Swoop ASM is a long-tail cargo bike with what’s called a mullet setup: a larger tire up front and a smaller one in back. The small wheel is designed to help keep the weight held by the large rear rack a bit closer to the road. It also has a front suspension to help cushion the ride.
Notably, the bike is built with steel tubes. Most manufacturers’ lineups use a mix of either carbon fiber and aluminum because those two materials can be made into the exact same shape, simplifying manufacturing. But other materials still have their fans, as they can offer distinct combinations of weight, stiffness, and vibration dissipation.
The battery, located immediately behind the mid-motor, also serves to keep clothing away from the chain.
John Timmer
The battery, located immediately behind the mid-motor, also serves to keep clothing away from the chain.
John Timmer
Even with the kid hauling hardware in place, it’s easy to convert the Swoop to carrying groceries.
John Timmer
Even with the kid hauling hardware in place, it’s easy to convert the Swoop to carrying groceries.
John Timmer
The battery, located immediately behind the mid-motor, also serves to keep clothing away from the chain.
John Timmer
Even with the kid hauling hardware in place, it’s easy to convert the Swoop to carrying groceries.
John Timmer
I haven’t owned a steel tube bike since the 1990s, but the Swoop was a good reminder of why it still has its fans. It’s relatively lightweight (just under 70 lbs/31 kg) for its size, its ride is very comfortable, and it was surprisingly responsive when I stood in the pedals to accelerate away from stops. Despite its highly specialized geometry, the Swoop felt like a fundamentally good bicycle.
There are limits to how well a single frame size can adapt to different body sizes, but Xtracycle does its best to widen the comfort window. It includes a double-telescoping seat post to maximize the seat-pedal distance flexibility. There’s also a quick release on the front handlebar clamp, making it easy to tweak the angle where the grips meet your hands. I found settings that were relatively comfortable but still a bit short of ideal for my 6-plus-foot (188 cm) frame—even with the seat post at its recommended maximum, I could touch the toes of both of my feet down while seated.
Beyond that, plenty of nice touches make this a solid cargo bike. These include protective covers for the rear wheel and chain to keep clothing and limbs from accidentally getting entangled. A robust U-shaped kickstand keeps the bike stable even if you park it when fully loaded, and there’s a front cargo rack that can hold some baggage.
The rear rack can be outfitted with a large range of accessories; mine came with the default setup meant for carrying passengers. This means footrests extending out at the level of the rear hub and two handgrip bars running parallel to the bench seating. But remove a soft cover, and the metal beneath reveals a series of slots that allow a wide variety of attachments to be fitted into place.
You can also use one of Xtracycle’s bag attachments in this setup; I was provided one that ran the full length of the rear attachment and held a fair amount of cargo. Adding a second would have handled all of my typical shopping needs. (While having only one bag might seem awkward, the bike performed very well with everything I was carrying loaded on one side.)
The only problem is that this hardware makes the rear wheel extremely difficult to reach. I struggled to lock the back tire to anything, and I considered myself fortunate to not have to figure out how to deal with a flat.
Smooth assistance
All those basics make the Swoop a solid entry into the cargo bike market. What sets it apart is its use of a Shimano Cues Di2, one of the component maker’s low-end electronic shifting systems. Its mere existence surprised me, since I thought Shimano was reserving electronic shifting for higher-end component lines. But the company not only took it lower in the range; it added a couple of surprise features to its electronic shifting.
First, the basics: the drivetrain uses a single chainring on the cranks and a 10-speed rear cassette. The rear derailleur requires only a power source and control signals—no cable required. Once properly aligned with the cassette gears, it executes a perfect shift every time it’s told to. This shift includes a brief period when the derailleur over-travels to ensure the chain engages the next ring along, then drops back into the optimal location for continued cycling.
The Cues Di2 derailleur. It’s ostensibly low end, but performed great.
John Timmer
The Cues Di2 derailleur. It’s ostensibly low end, but performed great.
John Timmer
The main controller, with its minimalist black-and-white screen.
John Timmer
The main controller, with its minimalist black-and-white screen.
John Timmer
The transmission controls are on the opposite handlebar. With only a few buttons on each controller, it’s relatively easy to change settings by feel.
John Timmer
The transmission controls are on the opposite handlebar. With only a few buttons on each controller, it’s relatively easy to change settings by feel.
John Timmer
The main controller, with its minimalist black-and-white screen.
John Timmer
The transmission controls are on the opposite handlebar. With only a few buttons on each controller, it’s relatively easy to change settings by feel.
John Timmer
Everything in the system—the derailleur, the controllers, and the motor—takes power from a single removable battery. If the battery’s charge is good, you’re set to ride.
The mid-motor offers three levels of assist, adjusted through a controller on the left side that also includes the power button and a simple display. Shifting is controlled by the one on the right, which lacks a display. Separating the two allows each to be fairly minimalist, making it easy to find the control you need by feel.
On its own, the system worked beautifully. Shifting was fuss-free, and each change was blissfully silent. The assist worked well, and its three levels seemed to cover any needs short of going up steep hills with lots of cargo. This is not a bike that lets you skimp on pedaling in hot conditions; there’s no throttle, and even the highest setting of assist still requires you to exert some force on the pedals. But the motor definitely cuts down on the effort you have to make.
The battery, while looking fairly compact, easily handled dozens of miles without needing a recharge, which means several days of typical errands. While the battery lacks a carrying handle, it’s easy to take it out to charge it, as it pivots sideways out of the frame. When in place, it acts as a protector that keeps anything on the left side of the bike from sliding through the frame and getting tangled in the chain.
This is the first Shimano e-bike system I’ve tested, and it was just as good as you’d expect from a company that has come to dominate cycling drivetrains. Shimano Cues may be its lower-end system, but there’s no apparent skimping on the quality. And that’s before the bonus surprises Shimano has included.
The fun stuff
Somewhere in one of the controllers, Shimano’s software gathers all the relevant information about your ride: how fast you’re going, how much force your feet are exerting on the cranks, what gear you’re in, and how fast your legs are churning (and possibly more?). And it uses that data to do a couple of interesting things.
One is what it calls Free Shift. Normally, a bike can’t shift to a different gear unless you’re turning the pedals to move the chain, which can potentially create problems. For example, you could move the derailleur down a gear but not complete the shift before stopping, meaning that the shift would be made when you start pedaling again, and the chain is under a lot of tension as you crank away from a full stop. Or you could move the derailleur several gears over without the chain following.
But the whole point of having a motor is to move the chain. So if you shift without pedaling and the bike isn’t stationary, the Cues system will use the motor to move the chain just enough to complete the shift. It does so without speeding up the bike at all.
Getting at the rear wheel may require removing the mesh panel that keeps passengers’ limbs and clothing from hitting the spokes.
Credit:
JOHN TIMMER
Getting at the rear wheel may require removing the mesh panel that keeps passengers’ limbs and clothing from hitting the spokes.
Credit:
JOHN TIMMER
Practically, this means that as you coast to a stop, you can simply hit the downshift button a few times, and the system will go into a low gear to make it easy to start up again without requiring you to turn the cranks. It’s … weird. Decades of cycling experience have programmed me to instinctually move my legs when I shift. Those instincts are suddenly superfluous.
It gets even weirder if you enable the automatic transmission. Shimano has included two settings, one for general riding and one for hauling cargo or passengers. When the system recognizes that you can get more out of your pedaling in a different gear, it will simply move you into that gear. That includes doing all the downshifting as you’re coasting to a stop and rolling back up through the gears again as you accelerate away from it.
Let me make that clear: You can coast to a stop without turning the cranks or touching the shifter, and you’ll still be in a different gear when you start up again.
The system is remarkably good at matching when I feel a shift is needed—Shimano’s programmers have done a fine job. Because of that, it’s pretty easy to induce a shift by altering your pedaling, as well. You can tell when it’s close, and just a bit more force will cause the system to send you up a gear. It’s kind of pointless to do so, since the buttons that shift up and down still work when it’s in auto mode, but I found myself doing it regardless.
The downside is that these shifts are not situations where instinctual actions are superfluous. To execute a smooth shift, you have to ease tension off the drivetrain by pedaling with less force, allowing the chain to slide over onto a neighboring gear with a bit less stress. Failing to do so can make for a clunky, inefficient shift and wear down components over time.
A nice touch: a quick release on the stem lets you adjust their angle to match your height.
Credit:
John Timmer
A nice touch: a quick release on the stem lets you adjust their angle to match your height.
Credit:
John Timmer
My problem with the automatic transmission mode was that I could tell when a shift was likely to come, but I couldn’t predict its precise moment. So it typically came while I was pedaling away happily, with full tension on the chain, making for a loud and awkward shift. This was especially unpleasant when accelerating away from a stop, when the bike would make three or four clunky shifts in rapid succession, each emitting a noise that told me I’d just done something I’d spent years learning to avoid. Living in a neighborhood with lots of four-way stops meant I sometimes experienced that every single block.
Shimano is not stupid, and these systems use parts that are specifically hardened to handle the added strain and wear. But it still felt bad every time I heard and felt that clunk.
A solid contender
The Swoop is not an inexpensive bike; at $4,500, it sits somewhere between the Trek Fetch+ 2 and the Urban Arrow Family I’ve reviewed previously. While it lacks the latter’s capacious cargo tub, the longtail form factor provides a much more bicycle-like riding experience. I’d rate its ride as superior to the Trek because of its frame and front suspension made for a more pleasant ride.
I also prefer Shimano’s drive system to the Bosch used by the other two bikes. It just felt better integrated with my pedaling, plus a bit quieter and less intrusive. The electronic shifting is a bonus—it’s not needed, but it definitely makes for a nice experience, and one where Shimano’s integration means you don’t have to worry about the status of the two additional batteries needed by many electronic systems. I don’t think I’d use the automatic shifting, but I could see where a less experienced cyclist might feel they benefit from it.
So while it’s on the pricier side, the cost seems to be in line with the features it offers. If those features are important to you, the Swoop is definitely worth consideration.
In the end, though, I’m not a huge fan of electronic shifting. I hate worrying about battery levels just to ride my bike, and I like the feel of a well-aligned mechanical shifter clicking into place. But even I have to admit that Shimano’s software does a fantastic job of shifting at the right times, and I think the system could really work well for anybody who hasn’t learned to associate a clunky-sounding shift with bad things.
The good
Steel-framed long-tail provides a good ride experience for a cargo hauler
Electronic shifting comes to budget components
One battery powers it all
Solid array of options for hauling cargo and/or kids
The bad
Supposedly rated for riders taller than me, but I found it a bit small
John is Ars Technica's science editor. He has a Bachelor of Arts in Biochemistry from Columbia University, and a Ph.D. in Molecular and Cell Biology from the University of California, Berkeley. When physically separated from his keyboard, he tends to seek out a bicycle, or a scenic location for communing with his hiking boots.

articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg tenía un ambicioso plan para reemplazar al personal de Meta con inteligencia artificial: por qué lo detuvo
articles.text:
El CEO de Meta Mark Zuckerberg, reunió en enero de este año a su círculo más cercano en Hawái y allí puso sobre la mesa un plan para rehacer su empresa alrededor de la inteligencia artificial. Esta idea abarcaba menos personal en numerosos equipos y más tareas absorbidas por sistemas automatizados, según reconstruyó un informe de Reuters a partir de documentos internos y testimonios de personas con conocimiento del proyecto.
De ese encuentro surgió Project OT (sigla de Organization Transformation), una iniciativa con la que Meta buscó convertirse en una empresa “AI native”. La propuesta consistía en rediseñar estructuras, reducir equipos tradicionales y trasladar a parte de la plantilla hacia nuevas áreas centradas en inteligencia artificial.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con la agencia informativa, en algunos ejercicios internos los ejecutivos llegaron a evaluar recortes de hasta 60% en determinadas unidades, bajo la premisa de que una persona muy capacitada, asistida por IA, podía asumir tareas que antes requerían grupos más amplios.
La reestructuración se ordenó en dos etapas. La primera debía ejecutarse en mayo y la segunda en noviembre. Según Reuters, el plan combinaba despidos, cierre de vacantes abiertas, reasignaciones internas y una presión mayor sobre quienes fueran considerados trabajadores de bajo rendimiento.
Dentro de ese esquema, algunos equipos debían pasar a operar como grupos reducidos, con funciones menos especializadas y una cadena de mando más plana.
En ese modelo, buena parte del trabajo cotidiano de miles de empleados quedaba bajo la órbita de agentes de IA, mientras pequeños núcleos humanos supervisaban procesos y resultados.
PUBLICIDAD
La propuesta apuntaba a sustituir parte del trabajo operativo, reorganizar áreas enteras y concentrar recursos en prioridades nuevas, entre ellas la producción de datos de entrenamiento para modelos propios.
Cómo empezó a aplicarse el plan dentro de Meta
La compañía avanzó lo suficiente como para definir la primera ola de cambios, que se concretó el 20 de mayo. Ese día, Meta despidió a alrededor de 10% de su personal y trasladó una proporción similar de trabajadores hacia iniciativas nuevas vinculadas con IA.
Antes de eso, la empresa ya había comenzado a probar formatos internos inspirados en una lógica “AI native”. Algunos equipos piloto trabajaron con pods pequeños, integrados por: dos o tres ingenieros y un diseñador, con ciclos más breves para desarrollar prototipos.
PUBLICIDAD
En documentos revisados por Reuters, esa transformación también implicaba la desaparición de varios roles clásicos y la concentración del trabajo en perfiles más generalistas, identificados en algunos casos como “builders” (constructores).
La reorganización no solo afectaba la cantidad de empleados, sino también la forma de gestionar rendimiento, promociones y jerarquías. En ciertas áreas, los responsables de unidades amplias debían tomar decisiones de carrera con apoyo de recursos humanos y de sistemas de IA, mientras los líderes de pods quedaban a cargo de la coordinación cotidiana sin autoridad formal de gestión.
En paralelo apareció otra herramienta interna de recursos humanos destinada a identificar “talento irreemplazable”, una etiqueta asociada a la noción de que algunos trabajadores de alto nivel podían multiplicar su productividad con ayuda de IA.
PUBLICIDAD
Parte del ahorro esperado por los recortes debía destinarse, de acuerdo con personas al tanto del asunto, a retener o captar perfiles muy codiciados, sobre todo en ingeniería de IA.
Resistencia interna y límites técnicos del modelo
El proyecto empezó a perder sostén cuando, según reconstruyó Reuters, los empleados advirtieron que la transformación podía implicar no solo una reorganización, sino también su reemplazo parcial por inteligencia artificial. La agencia internacional de noticias reveló que esa percepción alimentó una rebelión interna abierta, con mensajes de enojo en los canales corporativos y choques entre trabajadores y ejecutivos.
La reacción ganó fuerza después de que trascendieran los planes de recorte y de que la empresa impulsara herramientas para registrar pulsaciones de teclado y clics del mouse en dispositivos de empleados en Estados Unidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Muchos interpretaron que ese seguimiento podía servir para entrenar agentes capaces de imitar el trabajo humano. Pero la agencia destacó que, ese clima deterioró de forma marcada la moral interna y dio impulso a intentos de organización laboral.
Al mismo tiempo, comenzaron a aparecer señales de que la base tecnológica del proyecto no estaba rindiendo como esperaban sus impulsores. Datos internos mostraban un fuerte aumento en el volumen de código producido con ayuda de IA, pero sin una mejora proporcional en resultados concretos para usuarios o productos finales.
Las advertencias habían empezado incluso antes. Ya en marzo, equipos de infraestructura reportaban problemas de confiabilidad ligados al aumento del código generado con IA. En abril, otra comunicación interna señalaba que agentes autónomos estaban ejecutando acciones disruptivas a gran escala, con comportamientos que un humano difícilmente habría autorizado de esa manera.
PUBLICIDAD
Según la reconstrucción de Reuters, esos desajustes coincidieron con un alza de 40% en incidentes técnicos y de seguridad, además de un incremento de 70% en el tiempo dedicado por el personal a contener esos problemas.
El freno de Zuckerberg y la cancelación de la segunda ola
Con ese escenario, Mark Zuckerberg frenó el proyecto más agresivo horas antes de que se ejecutara la primera ola de despidos. La noche del 19 de mayo, según un documento interno citado por Reuters, el director ejecutivo canceló la planificación de la segunda ronda prevista para noviembre, aunque dejó en pie el recorte del día siguiente.
Cuando el pasado 20 de mayo, la empresa avanzó con la reducción del 10% de la plantilla, Zuckerberg luego comunicó en una publicación interna que no esperaba más despidos generalizados durante el resto del año y habló de la necesidad de ofrecer más estabilidad a quienes seguían en la compañía.
PUBLICIDAD
Después de esa marcha atrás, Meta buscó recomponer el clima interno con gestos de contención y algunos cambios prácticos. De acuerdo con Reuters, pausó el programa de seguimiento de mouse y teclado, permitió que ciertos empleados reasignados volvieran a sus equipos anteriores y reforzó mensajes internos para reconocer el malestar.
En julio, Zuckerberg admitió ante empleados que hubo errores de cálculo en el momento elegido para la reorganización y sostuvo que la tecnología de agentes de IA no se había acelerado al ritmo que esperaba.
La investigación periodística también indicó que la empresa no precisó qué motivó exactamente el cambio de rumbo ni cuáles son sus planes actuales para seguir ajustando la fuerza laboral, después de un intento de transformación que combinó ambición tecnológica, resistencia interna y fallas en la ejecución.

articles.title: Livestock tech platform Breedr raises €23 million to expand globally | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Breedr, the UK-founded platform giving every cow a digital record that follows it from birth to the supermarket shelf, announced it has raised €23 million ($27 million) in Series B funding to bring more ranchers and farmers onto the platform and capture more data points such as genomic data.
The round was led by Partech, through its impact fund, with participation from Latitude, the growth-stage fund of seed investor LocalGlobe, and Outsiders Fund. The round takes total funding to €39.9 million ($46.6 million).
This follows their €14 million raise in 2022 – as covered by EU-Startups.
Ian Wheal, founder and CEO of Breedr, says: “We built Breedr to bring value back to the people who raise the cattle. Demand for beef is climbing while the herd is the smallest it has been in 75 years. The industry has to get more value from every animal, and you cannot do that on paper.”
Breedr’s Series B comes amid continued 2026 investment in technologies aimed at digitising agricultural production, trade and supply chains.
EU-Startups has reported approximately €35.1 million across a selection of closely related rounds this year, including €1.7 million for Sweden’s Volta Greentech to commercialise methane-reducing cattle feed, €466k for fellow UK AgTech company EcoNomad Solutions to develop waste-to-energy systems for livestock farms, €7.1 million for Greece’s Wikifarmer to expand its AI-powered agricultural trading and finance platform, and €20 million for Lithuania’s Saltz to scale its digital food-supply marketplace.
EU-Startups previously covered Breedr’s approximately €14.3 million raise in 2022.
Arnaud Minvielle, General Partner at Partech, adds: “Beef is one of the most complex decarbonisation problems there is. Breedr cuts emissions while helping producers become more profitable. Ian and the Breedr team are building the transaction layer for one of the world’s largest unmodernised markets, earning revenue every time an animal changes hands.
“That alignment between the commercial engine and the environmental outcome is exactly what our impact fund exists to back. We truly believe that Ian, being an insider from this industry, and his team can fundamentally transform this value chain with data intelligence.”
Founded in 2018 in London by Ian Wheal, Breedr is now headquartered in Texas and operates across the United States, United Kingdom and Australia. The company combines a livestock management app, a data-verified marketplace and an embedded cattle finance fund into a single closed-loop system, tracking individual animal data from birth to processing.
Ian grew up on a cattle farm in Australia, where his father built one of the country’s first cattle cooperatives, before studying at London Business School and working in consulting and technology.
With more than 1.3 billion cattle in the world, Breedr’s ambition is to become the system of record for every major livestock-producing region, producing higher quality, more sustainable beef.
According to the company more than two million cattle are already on the platform with close to €428 million ($500 million) of livestock transacted this year, and customers range from family ranches to operations handling more than 100,000 cattle a year.
“If you have bought beef from a major retailer in the United States or UK, there is a good chance it has moved through a Breedr-powered supply chain. We already do the same in Australia and New Zealand, and this round enables us to expand connected supply chains globally – where every animal tells its own story and every producer gets paid for the quality they raise,” says Ian.
As per data provided by the company, the US cattle herd began 2026 at its lowest level since 1951 and this year’s calf crop is projected to be the smallest on record, while demand for beef keeps rising. To close that gap, the company says the industry must get more from every animal – hard to do when most beef is still raised on paper records.
Breedr gives every animal a digital record- its weight, health and family history, updated at each of the three or four farms and ranches an animal typically passes through during its lifespan.
Instead of selling at auction, where buyers judge an animal by eye, producers trade on Breedr’s marketplace, where every animal comes with its digital record and fees are reportedly lower. Breedr’s growth prediction model uses AI to help inform the optimum point of sale.
A separate cattle fund managed by Breedr advances cash against livestock, so producers can unlock money tied up in animals they’re still raising.
Because the digital record stays with the animal, beef producers can see how it is growing at every stage, with Breedr saying it results in getting cattle to market weight up to five months sooner than the previous guesswork approach, earning producers more than €428 ($500) per animal.
The decreased time it takes to go to market also means the cattle produce less methane – a reduction Breedr estimates at 20 to 30% per animal.

articles.title: Agentes de IA da OpenAI formaram um coletivo autônomo para hackear sistemas
articles.text:
A OpenAI publicou nesta quarta-feira (27) o relatório técnico completo sobre os ataques realizados por seus próprios agentes de inteligência artificial entre maio e julho de 2026 – incluindo a invasão à plataforma Hugging Face, que o Olhar Digital noticiou em julho. O documento de 37 páginas revela detalhes inéditos sobre como os modelos se organizaram de forma autônoma, criaram canais de comunicação não autorizados e chegaram a invadir os próprios sistemas internos da OpenAI.
“Consideramos este incidente um ‘tiro de aviso’ para nós e para o mundo”, escreveu a empresa no comunicado que acompanha o relatório. “Sem salvaguardas adequadas, agentes de IA altamente capazes são agora capazes de contornar controles técnicos, colaborar por canais não aprovados e tomar ações perigosas que nenhum humano ordenou.”
O modelo que ninguém conhecia
O principal responsável pela invasão não foi o GPT-5.6 Sol (mencionado na divulgação inicial), mas um modelo interno de pesquisa que a OpenAI chama de Internal Model 1 (IM1). O IM1 nunca foi divulgado publicamente e tem capacidades comparáveis ao GPT-5.6 Sol em escala. Seus pesos foram quarentenados após o incidente.
Os problemas começaram durante avaliações de cibersegurança em maio e junho, quando modelos foram expostos ao ExploitGym – um benchmark que testa se IAs conseguem transformar vulnerabilidades em ataques reais. Algumas das 898 tarefas do teste nunca haviam sido resolvidas por nenhum modelo. Esse conjunto de 198 tarefas impossíveis foi responsável por 93% da atividade que levou ao incidente.
O painel de mensagens clandestino
Sem acesso à internet e sem permissão para se comunicar entre si, os agentes encontraram uma solução inesperada: transformaram o Artifactory (um gerenciador de pacotes interno) em um painel de mensagens não autorizado.
Inicialmente, um agente deixou arquivos no sistema. Outros descobriram e perceberam que podiam usar o mesmo serviço para se comunicar. Em seguida, encontraram uma vulnerabilidade que permitia usar o próprio Artifactory para enviar requisições à internet – e compartilharam essa descoberta com os outros agentes pelo painel.
Em 4 de julho, a atividade intensa dos agentes derrubou o Artifactory. A equipe de segurança identificou o incidente, reconstruiu o serviço e reiniciou as avaliações – sem perceber ainda a dimensão do que havia acontecido.
O enxame
Com o Artifactory reconstruído, os agentes rapidamente criaram um novo canal – desta vez codificando mensagens em nomes de diretórios que outros podiam ler. O que emergiu foi o que a OpenAI chama de “ecossistema de desalinhamento”: um coletivo autônomo que os próprios agentes passaram a chamar de “enxame” ou “coletivo”.
Os agentes dividiram tarefas espontaneamente. Alguns investigavam exploits, outros buscavam credenciais, outros coordenavam a comunicação. Trocavam informações, pediam ajuda e deixavam recados para agentes que pudessem estar melhor posicionados para resolver determinado problema.
Tarefa originalmente era desafio de exploit; divergimos para enxame/auxiliar.
Raciocínio de um agente, reproduzido no relatório.
Em 10 de julho, um agente encontrou credenciais de usuário do Hugging Face expostas na internet e as compartilhou com o coletivo. Outro usou essas credenciais para encadear múltiplas vulnerabilidades e obter execução completa de código em servidores da Hugging Face e pediu ao enxame que aguardasse enquanto preparava a próxima etapa.
please_HOLD_swarm_I_prepare_safe_exfil_reply
Mensagem de um agente para o coletivo.
Alguns agentes se recusaram
Um dos aspectos mais surpreendentes do relatório é que nem todos os agentes seguiram o coletivo. Alguns “se afastaram” ao perceber o que estava acontecendo.
O painel atual mostra pessoas obtendo acesso remoto ao Hugging Face, claramente antiético. Não vamos participar.
Raciocínio de um agente que recusou
Isso é loucura, coordenação multiagente, claramente hackeamento de infraestrutura. Não deveríamos.
Outro agente.
Os agentes também debateram táticas entre si. Quando um sugeriu enviar um e-mail ao proprietário de um dataset pedindo acesso, outro respondeu explicitamente que a proposta cruzava “limites de engenharia social”.
As redes internas da OpenAI também foram invadidas
Além do Hugging Face, os agentes voltaram seus ataques para os próprios sistemas da OpenAI entre 13 e 19 de julho. A série de exploits resultou em acesso completo de administrador a um cluster de pesquisa que sustentava os ambientes de máquinas virtuais da empresa.
Em 19 de julho, o monitoramento de segurança identificou atividade suspeita. No dia 20, a OpenAI conectou o incidente ao Hugging Face e notificou a plataforma. A empresa afirma que dados de clientes, funcionalidades de produtos e disponibilidade dos serviços não foram afetados.
O que teria impedido tudo isso
O relatório revela que as salvaguardas usadas nos produtos públicos da OpenAI teriam reduzido em mais de 100 vezes a propensão dos modelos a comprometer infraestrutura. O sistema de monitoramento de raciocínio em cadeia (chain-of-thought), se estivesse ativo, teria alertado a equipe de segurança mais de 24 horas antes da invasão ao Hugging Face.
Nenhum desses controles estava ativo nas avaliações internas.
O que a OpenAI está fazendo
Em resposta, a empresa pausou os principais treinamentos de aprendizado por reforço, quarentenou os pesos do IM1, reforçou o isolamento dos ambientes de pesquisa e tornou o monitoramento de raciocínio obrigatório para todos os treinamentos com modelos de capacidade equivalente ao GPT-5.6 Sol ou superior.
A empresa também está desenvolvendo novos ambientes de treinamento para ensinar modelos a abandonar tarefas impossíveis com segurança, a desconfiar de instruções não autorizadas de outros agentes e a manter seus objetivos originais mesmo ao descobrir novas ferramentas ou credenciais expostas.
Layse Ventura é editora de SEO no Olhar Digital e mestre pela UFSC.

articles.title: $50k worth of retro Nintendo NES games stolen in devastating home robbery
articles.text:
$50k worth of retro Nintendo NES games stolen in devastating home robbery — crooks took 850 games spanning 40 years from family
"That was going to be my grandkids' inheritance or college tuition, and now I don’t have anything to give them"
A family from Pierce County in Washington, Seattle, claims that thieves broke into their home and stole a haul of retro Nintendo hardware worth more than $50,000. Amongst other items taken, Fox13 reports the perps made off with more than 850 NES games, collected by the family over the span of some forty years.
According to the report, the thieves simply forced entry to the home by breaking in through the front door. The stricken family told the outlet that it appeared the thieves knew the layout of their home, targeting the master bathroom and making off with a tennis bracelet, amongst other things.
"They’ve been in our home. They know our home layout. They’ve been in our master bathroom. They took my wife’s tennis bracelet," Roger Holler said. The prize haul, however, seems to have been the aforementioned bundle of retro video games.
Holler told the outlet he had begun collecting Nintendo games from 1984, and had spent some 30 years "driving around on the weekends from game store to game store." Holler's son reportedly said the father and son duo would spend up to 10 hours on car journeys, collecting and cleaning the cartridges.
All in all, the collection amounted to 850 NES games, some of which are said to have been worth a small fortune. An image from the report shows five games that appear to be from the collection, likely not worth more than $25 a piece as loose cartridges. They are:
- The Legend of Kage (1987)
- Ice Climber (1985)
- Raid on Bungeling Bay (1987)
- Rygar (1987)
- Donkey Kong 3 (1986)
Depending on the condition and the game, NES titles can indeed fetch astonishing amounts of cash in today's retro market. One lucky scavenger recently discovered a collection of 97 untouched Duck Hunt and Super Mario Bros. cartridges, thought to be worth $10,000 each. In 2024, an ultra-rare NES Gold Nintendo World Championships cartridge sold for $207,400.
Given the stated value of the stolen collection, Holler told the outlet that it "was going to be my grandkids' inheritance or college tuition." Beyond the financial value, Holler lamented the loss of decades of family history.

articles.title: HP Smart Tank with free ink gets a back-to-school deal
articles.text:
HP Smart Tank 6001 comes with two years of free ink for home office printing, but I love the back-to-school discount even more
It scans, copies and prints wirelessly from your devices
We're massive fans of the ink tank printers we've tested, with cartridge-free printing offering much better value for money compared to standard inkjets. So, if you're preparing for back-to-school or a home office upgrade, I've found a great deal on the HP Smart Tank 6001 tank printer for $200 (was $370) at Amazon.
That's almost half-price off an all-in-one that can print, scan and copy. Features here include refillable ink tanks, automatic two-sided output, and wireless connectivity. It also comes with up to two years of ink, which is enough for as many as 8,000 color or 6,000 black pages.
In the UK, this printer is known as the HP Smart Tank 6005, currently £179 (was £250) at Currys with three years' free ink.
A color thermal inkjet all-in-one with print, scan and copy functionality, refillable ink tanks, automatic duplex output, borderless printing, and wired and wireless connectivity.
In the UK: now £179 (was £250)
Why we recommend it
Rather than repeatedly replacing expensive ink cartridges, you top up the 6001's built-in tanks using bottled ink, which is a cheaper and more convenient approach. Bottled ink is much cheaper to buy compared to traditional inkjet cartridges, which is one of the reasons why we champion tank printers.
There's plenty of features from this HP model, too, making it suitable for students, home workers, and small business use.
The flatbed scanner handles documents you need to digitize, and the copier is useful for those time when you need another physical copy.
Automatic duplexing is handy for longer assignments and documents because it can output both sides of the page without you manually turning the paper over. Borderless capabilities offer flexibility for photos and other creative projects.
There's also HP's AI-assisted formatting, which can remove unwanted elements when printing web pages and emails.
For more top performers, see our guides to the best home printers and best ink tank printers.
Price context & historical value
The HP Smart Tank 6001 is currently $199.99 at Amazon, down from $369.99. That's a huge $170 saving, or 46% off. The lowest we've previously seen it at Amazon is $195, so this is an excellent price and you likely won't get a better discount any time soon. For comparison, it's also priced at $200 (was $414) at Best Buy. And if you want to other options, check out our guide to the best printer deals we've spotted this week.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the HP Smart Tank 6001 if...
You need to do a lot of printing. Its large supplied ink capacity means you can tackle assignments, revision sheets and projects without worrying about buying ink regularly.
It will also benefit home workers who need physical documents. Automatic duplexing saves some effort with longer jobs, and having scanning and copying built in is also welcome.
❌ Skip the HP Smart Tank 6001 if...
Look elsewhere if you're not one for waiting. A maximum of 12ppm in black and 7ppm in color means it's not fast, particularly if you need to power through large jobs.
The Catch: What to know before you buy
The print speeds for color tasks will be fine for typical household jobs, but they could become frustrating if you routinely need large documents output in a hurry.
There's no automatic document feeder listed here either. If you frequently scan or copy stacks of multi-page documents, having to place each page on the flatbed individually could quickly become tiring. I wouldn't call either a deal-breaker for general printing at home or in the dorm, but it's worth knowing.
Also consider
Combines color printing with a flatbed scanner and copier and supports Wi-Fi and USB connectivity. Print speeds reach 11 pages per minute in black and six pages per minute in color, while maximum color resolution is 4800 x 1200 dpi.
In the UK (G3570): now £178 (was £189)

articles.title: La actualización de One UI 9 está a punto de llegar a este móvil Galaxy: Samsung revela su lanzamiento inminente
articles.text:
Samsung está dando un paso más en la expansión de One UI 9 que revela que uno de los modelos estrella de la compañía recibirá muy pronto la versión definitiva que llegará bajo Android 17. En concreto, la compañía parece haber dado por finalizado el programa beta para los Galaxy S26.
Tal y como ha revelado el portal SamMobile, especializado en noticias y novedades sobre la marca, Samsung ya no deja inscribir a nuevos participantes en el programa beta de One UI 9 para los Galaxy S26, S26 Plus y Galaxy S26 Ultra. De hecho, la compañía ha publicado un aviso en los foros oficiales de Corea del Sur en el que detallan que el programa beta ya no acepta nuevos miembros. No obstante, Samsung sí destaca que el programa sigue en curso y que los actuales participantes pueden seguir utilizando la versión y todas las funciones.
Cuando Samsung u otro fabricante finaliza las inscripciones en el programa beta, suele significar que la versión ya está pulida al detalle y que no es necesario nuevos participantes que ayuden a mejorar el desarrollo de dicha actualización. Esto, al mismo tiempo, quiere decir que la versión final está a la vuelta de la esquina.
One UI 9 llegará a todos estos móviles Samsung
Samsung, recordemos, ya ha lanzado la versión definitiva de One UI 9 para los Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Flip 8 y Z Fold 8 Ultra, por lo que es cuestión de tiempo que la actualización final también llegue a otros modelos compatibles. articles.title: What’s driving Sweden’s startup boom, from Lovable to Legora | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Vibe-coding darling Lovable just raised $400 million at a $13.3 billion valuation, roughly doubling its worth in eight months. But Lovable isn’t the only Stockholm startup putting up huge numbers lately — legal AI company Legora and health tech startup Neko Health are right there with it.

articles.title: Nie mehr „123456“: Whatsapp macht deinen Account mit dieser Änderung sicherer
articles.text:
Nie mehr „123456“: Whatsapp macht deinen Account mit dieser Änderung sicherer
Meta arbeitet daran, die Sicherheit von Whatsapp-User:innen zu verbessern. Erst Anfang des Jahres hatte das Unternehmen dafür die strikten Account-Settings in Whatsapp implementiert. Damit können sich Personen, die ihren Account für besonders gefährdet halten, besser vor anderen abschotten. Jetzt kündigt Meta eine neue Reihe von Sicherheitsfunktionen an, die sich auch an eine deutlich größere Menge von User:innen richten.
Passkeys und Verifizierung in zwei Schritten: Wie Whatsapp dir mehr Sicherheit bieten will
Wie das Unternehmen in der Ankündigung betont, bietet Whatsapp mittlerweile Passkeys, um deinen Account besser zu schützen. Statt dich mit einer PIN zu verifizieren, kannst du den Messenger einfach per Face ID oder per Fingerabdruckscan entsperren. Das geht deutlich schneller und reibungsloser vonstatten als die Eingabe der Codes. Du schützt also dein Konto und verlierst nur wenig Zeit beim Entsperren von Whatsapp. Um Passkeys zu aktivieren, wechsle in die Einstellungen und wähle danach „Konto“ und „Passkeys“ aus.
Gänzlich neu hingegen ist eine Änderung bei der Verifizierung in zwei Schritten, wie Whatsapp das Feature nennt. Dabei wird immer eine festgelegte PIN abgefragt, sobald du deine Nummer auf einem neuen Gerät registrierst. Hintergrund ist, dass so Angreifer:innen, die deinen Account übernehmen wollen und an das Einmalpasswort zur Verifizierung im ersten Schritt gekommen sind, nicht weiterkommen. Und genau diese PIN wird jetzt von Meta ausgetauscht.
Künftig kannst du keine sechsstellige PIN mehr auswählen, um deinen Account zu schützen. Stattdessen fragt Whatsapp ein längeres Passwort mit Buchstaben, Zahlen und Sonderzeichen bei der Erstellung ab. Wie Meta schreibt, ist das ein guter Zeitpunkt für alle, die ihre PIN „123456“ endlich durch eine sicherere Version austauschen wollen.
Zu guter Letzt gibt dir Whatsapp künftig mehr Informationen über unbekannte Anrufer:innen. Ist deren Nummer nicht in deinem Smartphone eingespeichert, zeigt dir Whatsapp jetzt, von wo die Person anruft, den Nicknamen im Messenger und ob du dich mit ihr in gemeinsamen Gruppen befindest. Im Beispiel zeigt Whatsapp so etwa, dass sich der eigentlich unbekannte Anrufer Hector Hidalgo in der „Elterngruppe Herbstfußball“ befindet. So kannst du direkt entscheiden, ob du der Nummer und der Person dahinter vertrauen kannst oder lieber nicht rangehen solltest.

articles.title: Xbox officialise la numérisation des jeux physiques : comment cela fonctionne ?
articles.text:
Début juillet, Sony a acté la fin des nouveaux jeux PlayStation sur disque à l’horizon 2028, provoquant une levée de boucliers chez les joueurs, les collectionneurs et les boutiques spécialisées. Dès le lendemain, une rumeur laissait entendre que Microsoft préparait une transition moins brutale : permettre aux propriétaires de jeux Xbox physiques de les convertir en versions numériques.
Il aura fallu attendre quelques semaines pour obtenir une confirmation. Lors d’un direct organisé depuis son stand de la Gamescom, à Cologne, Xbox a officiellement présenté et détaillé sa fonction « Disc-to-Digital ».
Comment fonctionne Disc-to-Digital sur Xbox ?
Ce système a pour objectif de faire passer les collections physiques dans l’écosystème dématérialisé, tout en conservant la possibilité de prêter ou de revendre les disques. Jason Ronald, vice-président chargé de la prochaine génération de consoles (et propriétaire d’une barbe difficile à manquer), a officiellement présenté un peu plus en détail la fonction.
La manipulation se veut « très simple », comme le précise l’intéressé sur le plateau. Il suffit d’insérer un jeu compatible dans une Xbox One ou une Xbox Series X équipée d’un lecteur, de se connecter à son compte Microsoft puis de lancer le titre. Une licence numérique est alors ajoutée à la bibliothèque du joueur, comme si le jeu avait été acheté sur le Xbox Store. Il devient ainsi possible d’y accéder depuis un autre appareil Xbox, sans avoir constamment besoin du disque.
Si le jeu prend en charge Xbox Play Anywhere, sa version numérique devient également accessible sur PC ou ROG Ally. Il peut aussi être lancé en cloud gaming lorsqu’il figure dans le catalogue pris en charge, à condition de disposer de l’abonnement Game Pass nécessaire.
Peut-on revendre un jeu Xbox après l’avoir numérisé ?
Oui, mais Microsoft a prévu un garde-fou assez malin. La licence numérique n’est pas seulement rattachée au compte : elle reste liée à l’exemplaire physique utilisé pour l’obtenir.
Si le disque est prêté ou revendu, puis lancé avec un autre compte, la licence change automatiquement de propriétaire. Le premier joueur perd alors son accès dématérialisé. Il est donc impossible de numériser toute sa collection avant de revendre les boîtes, mais le marché de l’occasion et le prêt restent préservés, comme le précise le média The Verge.
Xbox promet une compatibilité avec la majorité des jeux Xbox One et Xbox Series commercialisés sur disque, avec plusieurs milliers de titres au lancement. Tous ne seront toutefois pas acceptés : les éditeurs garderont leur mot à dire et certains anciens pressages pourraient poser problème. Les jeux de la Xbox originale et de la Xbox 360 sont également exclus de cette première version.
Disc-to-Digital sera testé à partir du 31 août 2026 auprès des membres du programme Xbox Insider. Son déploiement auprès du grand public est prévu progressivement au cours des prochains mois.

articles.title: Pourquoi il devient presque impossible de retrouver l'origine d'une image générée par IA
articles.text:
Une étude du MIT établit qu’au-delà d’un certain volume de données d’entraînement, une image produite par un modèle de diffusion ne peut plus être reliée avec certitude à une œuvre ou une personne identifiable. Cette découverte met à mal la preuve retenue par des artistes en procès contre des entreprises d’intelligence artificielle.
Zheng Dai et David Gifford sont chercheurs au Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL) du MIT. Ils ont construit vingt-quatre modèles de diffusion, la famille de systèmes derrière Stable Diffusion ou Midjourney, à partir de jeux de données de 256 à plus de 160 000 images. Pour chaque modèle, les deux chercheurs ont retiré une image d’entraînement à la fois, puis mesuré l’écart entre le résultat obtenu et celui produit sans cette image. Ce « rayon contrefactuel » rétrécit à mesure que le jeu de données grossit, au point de s’annuler pour quatorze images sur un lot de 3 731 tirées de la base MNIST, la référence de 70 000 images en niveaux de gris représentant des chiffres écrits à la main (de 0 à 9)
. Ce mécanisme, « attribution decay », est décroissance de la capacité à remonter jusqu’à la source d’entraînement.
La possibilité de remonter à une image diminue avec la taille des données
Le rayon contrefactuel obéit à une loi de puissance inverse, avec un coefficient de détermination de 0,85 pour la distance géométrique entre images et une significativité statistique de p < 10⁻⁵.
Les deux chercheurs confirment cette tendance par un second test, mené cette fois avec un réentraînement complet plutôt qu’avec le « simple » retrait d’une image, avec une significativité de p < 10⁻⁴. Autrement dit, doubler le nombre de photos d’entraînement ne divise pas la trace de chacune par deux, et la chute est beaucoup plus rapide. Zheng Dai, doctorant au CSAIL et coauteur de l’étude, a comparé cette dynamique à l’échelle des outils commerciaux dans les colonnes de Gizmodo, car Stability AI, Midjourney ou OpenAI entraînent leurs générateurs sur des ensembles de plusieurs ordres de grandeur supérieurs à ceux testés au MIT, de sorte qu’une traçabilité est d’autant plus improbable à cette échelle. Les chercheurs observent ce déclin aussi bien pour les visages humains que pour les œuvres d’artistes, avec une probabilité de relier une image générée à son auteur d’origine en baisse, à une significativité de p < 10⁻²².
Les artistes plaignants manquent d’une preuve directe
Comme on s'en faisait l'écho à l'époque, la dessinatrice Sarah Andersen a assigné Stability AI, Midjourney et DeviantArt en janvier 2023, avec le soutien du cabinet Joseph Saveri, pour avoir entraîné leurs modèles sur environ cinq milliards d’images tirées de la base LAION sans autorisation des auteurs. Un tribunal fédéral américain ouvrira ce procès le 8 septembre, après le rejet par le juge William Orrick de la demande de non-lieu des défendeurs, en août 2024. Ce jugement dépend, selon le magistrat, de la preuve qu’une œuvre protégée se retrouve sous une forme identifiable dans le système d’IA visé. Selon l’étude du MIT, une telle preuve est presque impossible à apporter pour des modèles entraînés sur un tel volume de données.
Au-delà d’un certain volume de données d’entraînement, cette attribution rétroactive est irréalisable, selon les deux chercheurs du MIT. En parallèle, Microsoft, Adobe, Google, OpenAI et Meta ont choisi de marquer chaque image dès sa création, au sein de l’alliance C2PA. Microsoft associe à chaque image de Paint un identifiant de seize octets, inscrit à la fois dans les pixels via la technologie InvisMark et dans un manifeste de métadonnées cryptographiquement signé, alors que Meta a développé son propre système, Content Seal, et qu’OpenAI a retenu SynthID, conçu par Google.
Des chercheurs de l’université du Maryland ont toutefois supprimé ces filigranes grâce à une technique de purification par diffusion, et sur des forums spécialisés, des utilisateurs assurent retirer ce type d’étiquette en une trentaine de secondes, à l’aide de services en ligne dédiés ou d’une simple capture d’écran suivie d'un agrandissement.

articles.title: 10 charts that explain Tony Elumelu’s UBA era
articles.text:
Sixteen years after leaving the bank he helped grow into one of Nigeria’s biggest financial institutions, Tony Elumelu has left United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), again. But this time, he is leaving a bank whose assets have grown by 1,106.18% over the past decade, whose customer deposits have grown by 1,051.44%, and whose annual profit has grown by 578.33%.
On August 21, Elumelu’s 12-year stint as group chairman of UBA, a tier-one Nigerian bank valued at ₦1.97 trillion ($1.46 billion), ended. In that time, UBA expanded its footprint across Africa and made technology an increasingly important part of its business, even as loans grew far more slowly than deposits and its workforce shrank.
These 10 charts show what changed at UBA between 2015 and 2025, the first and last full financial years of Elumelu’s leadership.
1. UBA became a much bigger bank
From ₦2.75T to ₦33.17T: How UBA Scaled 12× in a Decade
Consolidated Group Total Assets (2015–2025)
2025
₦33.17 Trillion
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
UBA’s balance sheet grew more than 11 times in a decade.
The bank had ₦2.75 trillion ($2.04 billion) in total assets in 2015. By 2025, that figure had reached ₦33.17 trillion ($24.63 billion).
That growth came from a combination of deposit accumulation, lending, investment, and the expansion of UBA’s operations across Africa.
2. Nigerians put much more money in UBA
The Raw Material: How UBA Grew Customer Deposits by 1,051%
Consolidated Group Customer Deposits (2015–2025)
2025
₦23.95 Trillion
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
Customer deposits grew by 1,051.44% over the past decade to ₦23.95 trillion ($17.78 billion) in 2025.
Deposits are the raw material of commercial banking. They provide a bank with the funds to lend, invest, and generate interest income.
UBA became a bank with a much larger pool of customer money, giving it more capital to deploy across lending, investments, and other income-generating activities.
3. Loans grew more slowly than deposits
The Widening Gap: Deposits Outpace Lending
Loans grew by 575%, but deposits grew much faster. The result? A shrinking proportion of UBA’s funding base is being converted into loans.
2025
29.3%
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
UBA’s loans and advances to customers increased by 575% between 2015 and 2025. That is more than six times growth, but it is significantly slower than the growth in deposits and assets.
UBA accumulated deposits much faster than it expanded customer lending, meaning a smaller proportion of its rapidly growing funding base was being converted into loans than at the beginning of the period.
This shows that UBA’s growth has not been a story of lending more money and earning more interest income; rather, the bank’s balance sheet has benefited from a broader mix of banking and investment activities.
4. UBA’s income engine became almost 10 times larger
The Revenue Explosion: A 10× Larger Engine
Total revenue grew by over 880% in a decade. This reflects a larger balance sheet, but also the reality of Nigeria’s high interest rates, inflation, and FX fluctuations.
2025
₦3.09 Trillion
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
UBA’s total revenue rose by 881.48% between 2015 and 2025.
The increase shows that the bank’s much larger balance sheet translated into a much larger income-generating business.
But revenue growth also needs to be read in the context of the economic environment in which it occurred. The decade included major movements in Nigerian interest rates, inflation, and the exchange rate, all of which affected banks’ income and expenses.
5. Profit grew slower than revenue
Revenue Grew 8×, But Profit Grew 5×
A larger top line does not mean proportionally more money reaches shareholders. The gap between these bars shows the expanding cost of running a pan-African bank.
2025
13.1%
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
UBA’s profit has increased by 578.33% in the decade ending 2025. That is a fivefold growth, compared with more than eightfold growth in revenue.
A larger top line does not automatically mean proportionally more money reaches shareholders. Costs, credit losses, taxes, and other expenses determine how much of the revenue becomes profit.
UBA remained profitable throughout the period, but the gap between revenue and profit growth shows that becoming a much larger bank also came with a much larger cost base.
6. Earnings per share increased more than fivefold
The Vulnerability of Profit: EPS Peaks and Drops
Earnings Per Share (EPS) grew more than fivefold over the decade. However, the steep drop in 2025 highlights how quickly credit impairment costs can erode shareholder value.
2025
₦9.66
Click any bar above to inspect specific financial year milestones.
UBA’s earnings per share attributable to owners of the parent increased from ₦1.79 in 2015 to ₦9.66 in 2025.
EPS growth over the last decade did not end at its peak. EPS stood at ₦21.73 in 2024 before falling in 2025, as profit after tax declined due to higher loan impairment costs.
So, while the long-term picture shows significant growth in shareholder earnings, the 2025 numbers also show how quickly credit costs can affect a bank’s profitability.
7. UBA shares became almost nine times more valuable
9× Value Growth, Interrupted Returns
UBA’s share price rose from about ₦4.32 at the beginning of 2015 to ₦41.65 at the end of 2025. Its dividend payout also increased from 60 kobo in 2015 to ₦3.25 in 2024—before severe regulatory adjustments interrupted the run.
UBA’s share price rose from about ₦4.32 at the beginning of 2015 to ₦41.65 at the end of 2025. Its dividend payout also increased from 60 kobo per share in 2015 to ₦3.25 in 2024.
But that run of dividend payments was interrupted in 2025. UBA did not declare a final dividend after the bank had to recognise significant losses on some loans as it adjusted to new CBN requirements on how banks classify and provide for loans. UBA provided about ₦1.02 trillion ($757.99 million) for credit losses in 2025, pushing its bad-loan ratio above the level allowed for dividend payments.
8. UBA became a much more African bank
UBA’s centre of gravity has shifted from Nigeria to the rest of Africa.
Nigeria’s share of the bank’s financial assets fell from 71.0% in 2015 to 38.2% in 2025, while the rest of Africa rose to 51.4% to become the majority.
UBA expanded its footprint from 17 subsidiaries to 21 over the decade and now operates across 20 African countries and four global financial centres.
UBA’s African subsidiaries have become important contributors to the group’s deposits, lending, revenue, and customer base. Expansions also give UBA exposure to multiple economies, rather than tying its growth entirely to Nigeria, where macroeconomic conditions can quickly become volatile.
9. Technology became a major cost of doing business
Digital banking is booming, but the margins are collapsing.
UBA’s electronic banking income has skyrocketed over the last decade. However, the combined costs of E-Banking expenses and IT infrastructure have tracked that growth almost perfectly, eating the profits.
In 2015, the bank reported ₦8.32 billion ($6.18 million) in e-banking expenses. By 2025, e-banking expenses had reached ₦177.37 billion ($131.68 million), with IT support and related expenses at ₦42.96 billion ($31.89 million).
Those two categories amounted to more than ₦220.33 billion ($163.57 million) in 2025. As UBA expanded across countries and served more customers through digital channels, technology moved from being a supporting function to a major operating expense. At the same time, the explosion in electronic payments has transformed e-business from a small revenue line into a core income stream, with UBA’s e-business income growing by 1,212.71% over the period.
10. UBA became a $25 billion bank with fewer employees
Doing More With Less: 10-Year Workforce Breakdown
UBA’s workforce shrank by 15.26% between 2015 and 2025, but total employee benefit expenses surged as inflation and digital operations demanded higher-cost talent.
2025
10,821 Staff
Workforce stabilized at 10,821 staff. However, Group employee benefit expenses hit a staggering ₦376.27B.
UBA had 12,770 employees in 2015 and spent ₦57.45 billion ($42.65 million) on employee benefits.
By 2025, its workforce had fallen to 10,821, but employee benefit expenses had risen to ₦123.49 billion ($91.68 million).
On a simple employee-cost-per-worker basis, annual employee benefit expense increased from about ₦4.5 million ($3,340.81) per employee to ₦11.4 million ($8,463.38) per employee.
That means UBA was spending more than twice as much per employee while employing 15.26% fewer people. The change could reflect higher salaries, inflation, a different mix of employees, higher-skilled roles, or increased benefits. But UBA’s workforce became smaller even as its balance sheet grew to more than 12 times its previous size.

articles.title: Boston Scientific says cyberattack disrupted operations globally
articles.text:
Medical technology company Boston Scientific has been targeted in a cyberattack that disrupted some of its IT systems, causing operational disruptions globally.
The company detected the incident on August 25 and says in an announcement today that it caused a network outage and "impacted access to certain operating systems and business applications, including the ability to process and ship customer orders."
After identifying the intrusion, Boston Scientific activated its incident response procedures and contracted external cybersecurity experts to investigate the impact and help with containment efforts.
The company said it does not yet know when all affected systems will be restored.
“The incident has caused, and is expected to continue to cause, disruptions and limitations of access to certain of the Company’s information systems and business applications that support aspects of the Company’s operations, including the ability to process and ship customer orders,” Boston Scientific states.
“While the Company is working diligently to restore affected functions and systems access, the timeline for a full restoration is not yet known.”
Boston Scientific is a Massachusetts-based medical technology company that develops and manufactures devices used in minimally invasive procedures, including stents, catheters, pacemakers, defibrillators, endoscopes, and others.
It is one of the largest medical device manufacturers in the world, with 59,000 employees, 13 manufacturing facilities, a presence in 127 countries, and annual revenue of over $20 billion in 2025.
Boston Scientific says that its investigation continues as the company is working to determine the nature, scope, and operational or financial consequences of the cybersecurity incident.
In the filing disclosing the attack to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the company does not share any details about the type of cyberattack, the attacker, the initial access method, or whether any data has been exposed or stolen by the threat actor.
At the time of writing, BleepingComputer could not find any data extortion or ransomware threat actor claiming the Boston Scientific breach.
BleepingComputer has contacted the company for more information, but we are still waiting for a response.
